Diusulkan dilewati: Arnapkapfaaluk adalah nama Sedna di kalangan Inuit Copper; artikelnya dialihkan ke Sedna, yang dikerjakan sebagai entri tersendiri (slug sedna, batch-142). (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedna_(mythology)).

claims.statement: The Pombero is a mythological being typical of Paraguay's heritage.
claims.statement_id: Pombero adalah makhluk mitologi khas warisan budaya Paraguay.
claims.quote: is a mythological being typical of Paraguay's cultural heritage.

claims.statement: It is a small humanoid creature of Guarani mythology.
claims.statement_id: Ia makhluk mitos bertubuh kecil mirip manusia dalam mitologi Guarani.
claims.quote: it is a mythical humanoid creature of small stature in Guarani mythology.

claims.statement: He is also called Pyrague ("hairy feet"), Karai Pyhare ("lord of the night") and Kuarahy Jára ("master of the sun").
claims.statement_id: Ia juga disebut Pyrague ("kaki berbulu"), Karai Pyhare ("penguasa malam"), dan Kuarahy Jára ("penguasa matahari").
claims.quote: Pyrague ("hairy feet"), Karai Pyhare ("lord of the night"), Kuarahy Jára ("master of the sun")

claims.statement: The legend, with those of other Guarani mythological figures, is an important part of the culture of a region stretching from northeast Argentina north through all of Paraguay into southern Brazil.
claims.statement_id: Legendanya, bersama tokoh mitologi Guarani lainnya, menjadi bagian penting budaya suatu wilayah yang membentang dari timur laut Argentina ke utara melintasi seluruh Paraguay hingga Brasil selatan.
claims.quote: The legend, along with those of other mythological figures of the Guarani, is an important part of the culture of a region stretching from northeast Argentina northward through the whole of Paraguay and into southern Brazil.

claims.statement: He is also known in the mythology of the Mbyá tribe of southern Brazil and the Argentinian province of Misiones, and as Cho Pombé ("Don Pombero").
claims.statement_id: Ia juga dikenal dalam mitologi suku Mbyá di Brasil selatan dan provinsi Misiones di Argentina, serta disebut Cho Pombé ("Don Pombero").
claims.quote: Also known in the mythology of the Mbyá tribe of southern Brazil and the Argentinian province of (Misiones) and Cho Pombé ("Don Pombero")

claims.statement: Pombero is said to be a primarily nocturnal creature.
claims.statement_id: Pombero konon terutama makhluk malam hari.
claims.quote: he is said to be a primarily nocturnal creature.

claims.statement: In some parts of Argentina he is known mainly by the Spanish translation of his name, Señor de la noche.
claims.statement_id: Di beberapa bagian Argentina ia terutama dikenal lewat terjemahan Spanyol namanya, Señor de la noche.
claims.quote: In some parts of Argentina he is known primarily by the Spanish translation of his name, Señor de la noche.

claims.statement: He is usually described as short and ugly, with very short arms and hairy hands and feet.
claims.statement_id: Ia biasanya digambarkan pendek dan buruk rupa, dengan lengan sangat pendek serta tangan dan kaki berbulu.
claims.quote: he is usually described as being short and ugly, with very short arms and hairy hands and feet.

claims.statement: His hairy feet are said to give him the ability to sneak up on people silently.
claims.statement_id: Kaki berbulunya konon memberinya kemampuan mendekati orang tanpa suara.
claims.quote: His hairy feet are said to give him the ability to sneak up on people silently

claims.statement: The Pombero generally dwells in rural areas, in the forest, though he sometimes inhabits an abandoned house, deserted rooms in an occupied home, or empty barns.
claims.statement_id: Pombero umumnya tinggal di daerah pedesaan, di hutan, meski kadang memilih menghuni rumah terbengkalai, kamar kosong di rumah berpenghuni, atau bahkan lumbung kosong.
claims.quote: The Pombero generally dwells in rural areas, living in the forest, although he will sometimes choose to inhabit an abandoned house, deserted rooms within an occupied home, or even empty barns.

claims.statement: As a forest dweller, the Pombero is said to imitate the sounds of various forest creatures, especially birdsong.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai penghuni hutan, Pombero konon dapat menirukan suara berbagai makhluk hutan, terutama kicau burung.
claims.quote: As a forest dweller, the Pombero is said to be able to imitate the sounds of various forest creatures. Most specifically it is believed that the Pombero can imitate birdsong

claims.statement: A common element of the myth in various Guaraní-based societies is that the Pombero protects birds from children who hunt them with slingshots.
claims.statement_id: Unsur yang umum dalam mitos di berbagai masyarakat berbasis Guaraní adalah bahwa Pombero melindungi burung dari anak-anak yang memburunya dengan ketapel.
claims.quote: One common aspect of the myth among various Guaraní based societies is that the Pombero protects the birds from children who hunt them with slingshots.

claims.statement: His favourite activities include setting cattle loose, stealing eggs, chicken and honey, frightening horses so they throw their riders, and scattering corn, rice or other provisions.
claims.statement_id: Kegemarannya antara lain melepaskan ternak, mencuri telur, ayam, dan madu, menakuti kuda hingga penunggangnya terlempar, serta menebar jagung, beras, atau bekal lain.
claims.quote: Among his favourite activities are setting loose cattle, stealing eggs, chicken and honey, frightening horses and causing them to throw their riders off, as well as scattering corn, rice, or other provisions.

claims.statement: The Pombero is generally viewed as a harmless troublemaker.
claims.statement_id: Pombero umumnya dipandang sebagai pembuat onar yang tidak berbahaya.
claims.quote: The Pombero is generally viewed as a harmless troublemaker.

claims.statement: The Pombero is hard, if not impossible, to detect because of his silent movements and other supernatural abilities, such as turning invisible or squeezing through impossibly narrow spaces.
claims.statement_id: Pombero sulit, bahkan hampir mustahil, dideteksi karena geraknya yang senyap dan kemampuan gaib lain, seperti menjadi tak terlihat atau menyelinap melalui celah yang mustahil sempit.
claims.quote: The Pombero is difficult, if not impossible, to detect due to his silent movements as well as other supernatural abilities, such as being able to turn invisible, squeeze through impossibly narrow spaces, or other such feats.

claims.statement: It is said one can keep the Pombero from mischief by leaving gifts, above all cigars and rum, though honey is also an acceptable offering.
claims.statement_id: Konon orang dapat mencegah Pombero berbuat usil dengan meninggalkan hadiah untuknya, terutama cerutu dan rum, meski madu juga persembahan yang diterima.
claims.quote: It is said that one can keep the Pombero from engaging in such mischief by leaving gifts out for him, most specifically cigars and rum, though honey is also an acceptable offering.

claims.statement: The Pombero tends to be the most widespread and pervasive mythological figure among Guaraní-speaking cultures today.
claims.statement_id: Pombero cenderung menjadi tokoh mitologi yang paling tersebar dan meresap di antara budaya penutur Guaraní saat ini.
claims.quote: The Pombero tends to be the most widespread and pervasive of mythological figures among Guaraní speaking cultures today.

claims.statement: Another figure of Guaraní mythology, Kurupi, is blamed in a similar way for unexpected or unexplained pregnancies.
claims.statement_id: Tokoh lain mitologi Guaraní, Kurupi, disalahkan dengan cara serupa atas kehamilan yang tak terduga atau tak terjelaskan.
claims.quote: Another character from Guaraní mythology, Kurupi, is blamed in a similar manner for unexpected or unexplained pregnancies.

claims.statement: In November 2020, Paraguayan game developer Inside Studios launched the video game "Pombero – The Lord of Night", which received mixed criticism.
claims.statement_id: Pada November 2020, pengembang gim Paraguay Inside Studios meluncurkan gim video "Pombero – The Lord of Night" yang menuai kritik beragam.
claims.quote: In November 2020, Paraguayan game developer Inside Studios launched the video game "Pombero – The Lord of Night", receiving mixed criticism.

claims.statement: The Pombero is the best-known duende (spirit being) in Paraguay, especially in the Guairá and Caazapá area.
claims.statement_id: Pombero adalah duende (makhluk halus) yang paling dikenal di Paraguay, terutama di kawasan Guairá dan Caazapá.
claims.quote: POMBÉRO es el duende más conocido en Paraguay, especialmente en la zona del Guairá y Caazapá.

claims.statement: He is the spirit of the night who whistles in the winds and can exactly imitate many animals, such as the horse, dog, hen, cow and especially chicks.
claims.statement_id: Ia adalah genius (roh) malam yang bersiul di angin dan dapat menirukan dengan tepat banyak hewan, seperti kuda, anjing, ayam, sapi, dan terutama anak ayam.
claims.quote: Es el genio de la noche que silba en los vientos y puede remedar exactamente a numerosos animales, como al caballo, al perro, a la gallina, a la vaca y, especialmente, a los pollitos.

claims.statement: He loves and defends animals and always lives invisible near people.
claims.statement_id: Ia mencintai dan membela hewan, serta selalu hidup tak terlihat di dekat manusia.
claims.quote: Ama y defiende a los animales y vive siempre invisible cerca de las personas.

claims.statement: He is a mischievous spirit, but bad to those who mock him; as revenge he pursues the animals of the house: horses, dogs, cows, hens and so on.
claims.statement_id: Ia genius yang jahil, tetapi jahat kepada orang yang mengejeknya; sebagai balasan ia mengejar hewan-hewan di rumah seperti kuda, anjing, sapi, dan ayam.
claims.quote: Es un genio travieso, pero malo con los que se burlan de él. Como venganza persigue a los animales de la casa, caballos, perros, vacas, gallinas, etc.

claims.statement: It is said one wins his friendship by leaving tobacco and cane liquor in the kitchen or at the window; in return he protects his friend and family, looking after the house and animals.
claims.statement_id: Konon orang memenangkan persahabatannya dengan meninggalkan tembakau dan caña (minuman keras tebu) di dapur atau jendela; sebagai balasan ia melindungi sahabat dan keluarganya dengan menjaga rumah dan hewan mereka.
claims.quote: se cuenta que uno gana su amistad dejándole en la cocina o en la ventana, tabaco y caña. En honor a esa generosidad amistosa el POMBÉRO ofrece a su amigo y familia una importante protección: le cuida el rancho y los animales.

claims.statement: He can turn into an Indian, a log, a creek stone, a dry tree, a camalote or tree roots, or fly off transformed into a carancho when he fears being discovered or is caught by daylight on open ground.
claims.statement_id: Ia dapat berubah menjadi orang pribumi, batang kayu, batu sungai, pohon kering, camalote, atau akar pohon, atau terbang dalam wujud carancho ketika takut ketahuan manusia atau didapati cahaya siang di tanah lapang.
claims.quote: Puede convertirse en indio, tronco, piedra de arroyo, árbol seco, camalote, raíces de árboles, o puede salir volando transformado en carancho, cuando teme ser descubierto por los hombres o le sorprende la luz del día en campo llano.

claims.statement: He only calms down if the person he pursues carries the prayer of Saint Michael the Archangel in a pocket.
claims.statement_id: Ia baru tenang jika orang yang dikejarnya membawa doa Santo Mikael Malaikat Agung di saku.
claims.quote: Solo se calma si su perseguido porta en el bolsillo la oración de San Miguel Arcángel, el capitán vencedor de todos los espíritus malignos.

claims.statement: According to scholars, Pombéro means "agazapado" (crouching).
claims.statement_id: Menurut para peneliti, Pombéro berarti "agazapado" (meringkuk).
claims.quote: Según los estudiosos, POMBÉRO significa: agazapado.

claims.statement: To this day most of the peasantry believes in this night spirit and fears him.
claims.statement_id: Hingga kini sebagian besar kaum tani percaya akan keberadaan roh malam ini dan takut kepadanya.
claims.quote: Hasta nuestros días, la mayoría del campesinado cree en la existencia de este genio nocturno y le tiene miedo.

claims.statement: In the interior, when night falls, people out of fear no longer say the name Pombéro but call him Señor de la Noche or Karai Pyhare.
claims.statement_id: Di pedalaman, ketika malam tiba, orang karena takut tidak lagi menyebut nama Pombéro, melainkan menyebutnya Señor de la Noche atau Karai Pyhare.
claims.quote: En el interior del país cuando llega la noche, la gente, por temor, ya no pronuncia el nombre del POMBÉRO, sino que le llama Señor de la Noche o KARAI PYHARE.

claims.statement: It is even said that during the War of '70 a "Batallón Pombéro" appeared, showing how popular this myth was.
claims.statement_id: Konon pada Perang '70 muncul sebuah "Batallón Pombéro" yang menggambarkan betapa populernya mitos ini.
claims.quote: Inclusive se habla que durante la Guerra del 70 apareció un "Batallón Pombéro" que pinta la gran popularidad de este mito.

claims.statement: The Pukwudgie is a mischievous or menacing dwarfish human-like creature of Native American lore.
claims.statement_id: Pukwudgie adalah makhluk kerdil mirip manusia yang jahil atau mengancam dalam cerita pribumi Amerika.
claims.quote: is a mischievous or menacing dwarfish human-like creature of Native American lore.

claims.statement: It is known especially from Wampanoag folklore in Massachusetts.
claims.statement_id: Ia terutama dikenal dalam cerita rakyat orang Wampanoag di Massachusetts.
claims.quote: It has become particularly known as part of the folklore of the Wampanoag people of Massachusetts

claims.statement: It was originally part of an Ojibwe folktale of the Great Lakes region.
claims.statement_id: Awalnya ia bagian dari dongeng orang Ojibwe di wilayah Great Lakes.
claims.quote: But it was originally part of the folktale of the Ojibwe people of the Great Lakes region

claims.statement: Shape-shifting Pukwudgies in their native form are said to be short, no more than knee-high (2–3 feet), gray-skinned, with very large noses, ears and fingers.
claims.statement_id: Pukwudgie yang bisa berubah wujud dalam wujud aslinya konon bertubuh pendek, tidak lebih dari setinggi lutut (2–3 kaki), berkulit abu-abu, dengan hidung, telinga, dan jari yang sangat besar.
claims.quote: The shape-shifting Pukwudgies in their native form are said to be short-statured, no more than knee-high (2–3 feet (0.61–0.91 m) tall), and gray-skinned, with very large noses, ears, and fingers.

claims.statement: They can transform into dangerous beasts (cougars or quilled porcupine), or appear and disappear at will; they may also have the power to harm people by staring them down.
claims.statement_id: Mereka dapat berubah menjadi binatang berbahaya (puma atau landak berduri), atau muncul dan menghilang sesuka hati; mereka juga mungkin dapat mencelakai orang dengan menatapnya tajam.
claims.quote: But they can transform into dangerous beasts (cougars or quilled porcupine), or appear and disappear at will. They may also have the power to bring harm to people by staring them down.

claims.statement: Pukwudgies are said to be the enemies of the culture heroes, the giant Maushop and his wife, Granny Squanit.
claims.statement_id: Pukwudgie konon musuh para pahlawan budaya, raksasa Maushop dan istrinya, Nenek Squanit.
claims.quote: Pukwudgies are said to be the enemies of culture heroes, the giant Maushop and his wife, Granny Squanit.

claims.statement: According to the Massachusetts Wampanoag myth, Pukwudgies were originally well-intentioned helper spirits, but they were bunglers and their efforts tended to backfire.
claims.statement_id: Menurut mitos Wampanoag di Massachusetts, Pukwudgie semula roh penolong yang berniat baik tetapi ceroboh sehingga usahanya sering berbalik merugikan.
claims.quote: According to the myth of the Massachusetts Wampanoag, Pukwudgies were originally well-intentioned helper spirits, except they were bunglers and their efforts tended to backfire.

claims.statement: While the Ojibwe are rather dismissive of the Little Folk as little more than pranksters, the Wampanoag warn against disrespecting Pukwudgies lest they fire poisoned arrows, lure victims to their deaths in the forest, push them off cliffs and start fires.
claims.statement_id: Orang Ojibwe cenderung menganggap Orang Kecil hanya sebagai penjahil, sedangkan Wampanoag memperingatkan agar tidak bersikap tidak hormat kepada Pukwudgie karena mereka dapat menembakkan panah beracun, memancing korban mati di hutan, mendorong mereka dari tebing, dan menyulut api.
claims.quote: Thus while the Ojibwe are rather dismissive of the Little Folk as little more than pranksters, the Wampanoag warn of disrespecting a Pukwudgies lest they fire their poisoned arrows, lure victims to their deaths in the forest, push them off cliffs, start fires

claims.statement: They are also said to attack their victims with short knives and spears, blind them with sand, and kidnap children.
claims.statement_id: Mereka juga disebut menyerang korban dengan pisau dan tombak pendek, membutakan korban dengan pasir, dan menculik anak-anak.
claims.quote: attack their victims with short knives and spears, use sand to blind their victims, as well as kidnapping children.

claims.statement: The Ojibwa folktale "Puck Wudj Ininee" in Schoolcraft's Algic Researches (1839) describes the origin of the little people, originally a single orphaned boy named Wa-Dais-Ais-Imid ("He of the Little Shell") who lived with his sister; he could become invisible.
claims.statement_id: Dongeng Ojibwa "Puck Wudj Ininee" dalam Algic Researches karya Schoolcraft (1839) menceritakan asal-usul orang-orang kecil, semula seorang anak yatim bernama Wa-Dais-Ais-Imid ("Dia dari Kerang Kecil") yang tinggal bersama adiknya; ia dapat menjadi tak terlihat.
claims.quote: The Ojibwa folktale in Schoolcraft's Algic Researches (1839) entitled "Puck Wudj Ininee" describes the origins of the little people, originally a single orphaned boy named Wa-Dais-Ais-Imid ("He of the Little Shell") who lived with his sister. He had the ability to become invisible.

claims.statement: Pukwudgie (literally "person of the wilderness", "little wild man of the forest") is also styled Pukwudgee.
claims.statement_id: Pukwudgie (secara harfiah "orang dari alam liar", "manusia liar kecil dari hutan") juga ditulis Pukwudgee.
claims.quote: 'person of the wilderness', 'little wild man of the forest'), also styled Pukwudgee

claims.statement: The term Pukwudgie is not attested as old usage in the Massachusetts area; the local natives did preserve folklore about the little people, but the original name they used in their New England languages is lost to history.
claims.statement_id: Istilah Pukwudgie tidak tercatat dipakai sejak lama di wilayah Massachusetts; penduduk asli setempat memang menyimpan cerita tentang orang-orang kecil, tetapi nama asli mereka dalam bahasa New England hilang ditelan sejarah.
claims.quote: The term Pukwudgie is not of attested old usage in the Massachusetts area, and although the local natives did had preserved folklore concerning the little people, the original name they were called by in their New England languages is lost to history

claims.statement: Encouraged by the poem's popularity, the name Pukwudgie and notions about them were subsequently "imported to Massachusetts".
claims.statement_id: Didorong popularitas puisi itu, nama Pukwudgie dan gagasan tentang mereka kemudian "diimpor ke Massachusetts".
claims.quote: Encouraged by the popularity of the poem, the name of Pukwudgie and notions about them were subsequently "imported to Massachusetts".

claims.statement: A version of Kwa-sind being killed by the "Puk-wudjees", moving the murder scene to a lake island in Middleboro, Massachusetts, was published in Thomas Weston's History (1906).
claims.statement_id: Versi Kwa-sind dibunuh oleh "Puk-wudjees" dengan memindahkan tempat pembunuhan ke sebuah pulau danau di Middleboro, Massachusetts, diterbitkan dalam History karya Thomas Weston (1906).
claims.quote: A version of Kwa-sind being killed by the "Puk-wudjees", displacing the murder scene to a lake island in Middleboro, Massachusetts was published in Thomas Weston's History (1906, detailed under § Literature below)

claims.statement: Later, Wampanoag natives crafted tales that deliberately borrowed the "Pukwudgie" and retold them for the purpose of Indian cultural awareness.
claims.statement_id: Kemudian orang Wampanoag membuat cerita yang sengaja meminjam "Pukwudgie" dan menuturkannya kembali demi menumbuhkan kesadaran budaya Indian.
claims.quote: Later, Wampanoag natives crafted tales that deliberately borrowed the "Pukwudgie", and retold them for the purpose of Indian cultural awareness.

claims.statement: The anthology of Cape Cod tales, Elizabeth Reynard's The Narrow Land (1934), included tales contributed by Chief Red Shell (Clarence Wixon), a member of the Mashpee Wampanoag Tribe.
claims.statement_id: Antologi cerita sekitar Cape Cod, The Narrow Land karya Elizabeth Reynard (1934), memuat cerita yang disumbangkan Kepala Suku Red Shell (Clarence Wixon), anggota Suku Mashpee Wampanoag.
claims.quote: Elizabeth Reynard The Narrow Land (1934), an anthology of tales around Cape Cod, included tales contributed by Chief Red Shell (Clarence Wixon), a member of the Mashpee Wampanoag Tribe.

claims.statement: The myth retold in Reynard's anthology later inspired Jean Fritz's children's book The Good Giants and the Bad Pukwudgies (1982).
claims.statement_id: Mitos yang dituturkan ulang dalam antologi Reynard kemudian mengilhami buku anak Jean Fritz, The Good Giants and the Bad Pukwudgies (1982).
claims.quote: The retold myth in Reynard's anthology later inspired Jean Fritz's children's book, The Good Giants and the Bad Pukwudgies (1982)

claims.statement: Mohegan lore speaks of the Mukheahweesug or Makiawisug as a similar forest spirit.
claims.statement_id: Cerita rakyat Mohegan menyebut Mukheahweesug atau Makiawisug sebagai roh hutan yang serupa.
claims.quote: The lore among the Mohegan people speak of the Mukheahweesug or Makiawisug as a similar forest spirit.

claims.statement: Among the Mi'kmaq (of Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island) the equivalent is known as the Mikumwess.
claims.statement_id: Di kalangan Mi'kmaq (Nova Scotia dan Pulau Pangeran Edward) padanannya disebut Mikumwess.
claims.quote: Among the Mi'kmaq (of Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island) the equivalent is known as the Mikumwess.

claims.statement: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow's poem The Song of Hiawatha (1855), Chapter XVIII, "The Death of Kwasind", tells of the death of the giant Kwasind at the hands of the Pukwudgies.
claims.statement_id: Puisi The Song of Hiawatha karya Henry Wadsworth Longfellow (1855), Bab XVIII "The Death of Kwasind", menceritakan kematian raksasa Kwasind di tangan Pukwudgie.
claims.quote: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow's poem The Song of Hiawatha (1855), Chapter XVIII, "The Death of Kwasind" tells of the death of the giant Kwasind by the Pukwudgies

claims.statement: In the poem the Puk-Wudjies are called mischievous and envious "Little People", fairies and pygmies, who plotted and conspired against Kwasind, whom no man could match.
claims.statement_id: Dalam puisi itu, Puk-Wudjies disebut jahil dan iri, "Orang Kecil", peri dan kurcaci, yang bersekongkol melawan Kwasind, yang tak tertandingi.
claims.quote: No man could compete with Kwasind. But the mischievous Puk-Wudjies, They the envious Little People, They the fairies and the pygmies, Plotted and conspired against him.

claims.statement: In the poem the Puk-Wudjies wait armed in their war encampment and hurl pine-cones down on Kwasind, striking his shoulders and his unprotected crown.
claims.statement_id: Dalam puisi itu, Puk-Wudjies menunggu bersenjata di perkemahan perang mereka dan melempari Kwasind dengan kerucut pinus hingga mengenai bahu dan kepalanya.
claims.quote: In his birch canoe came Kwasind, ... Underneath the war encampment Of the pygmies, the Puk-Wudjies. There they stood, all armed and waiting, Hurled the pine-cones down upon him, Struck him on his brawny shoulders, On his crown defenceless struck him.

claims.statement: The poem's glossary explains Puk-Wudj'ies as "little wild men of the woods; pygmies".
claims.statement_id: Glosarium puisi itu menerangkan Puk-Wudj'ies sebagai "manusia liar kecil dari hutan; kurcaci".
claims.quote: Puk-Wudj'ies, little wild men of the woods; pygmies

claims.statement: In the poem the only weapon that could wound and slay Kwasind was the seed-cone of the pine-tree and the blue cone of the fir-tree.
claims.statement_id: Dalam puisi itu, satu-satunya senjata yang dapat melukai dan membunuh Kwasind adalah kerucut biji pohon pinus dan kerucut biru pohon cemara.
claims.quote: Now this wondrous strength of Kwasind In his crown alone was seated ... Even there the only weapon That could wound him, that could slay him, Was the seed-cone of the pine-tree, Was the blue cone of the fir-tree.

claims.statement: Xelhua is one of seven Aztec giants who escaped the flood by climbing the mountain of Tlaloc and then built the Great Pyramid of Cholula.
claims.statement_id: Xelhua adalah salah satu dari tujuh raksasa dalam mitologi Aztek yang selamat dari air bah dengan mendaki gunung Tlaloc, lalu membangun Piramida Besar Cholula.
claims.quote: Xelhua is one of the seven giants in Aztec mythology who escaped the flood by ascending the mountain of Tlaloc in the terrestrial paradise and afterwards built the Great Pyramid of Cholula.

claims.statement: He is one of the six giant sons of Mixcoatl, personification of the Milky Way.
claims.statement_id: Ia salah satu dari enam raksasa putra Mixcoatl, personifikasi Bima Sakti.
claims.quote: One of the six giants sons of Mixcoatl, the personification of the Milky Way

claims.statement: The first-born, the giant Xelhua, of Itzocan and Epatlan, and Cuauquechollan, the cities he founded.
claims.statement_id: Putra sulung, raksasa Xelhua, dari Itzocan dan Epatlan, serta Cuauquechollan, kota-kota yang didirikannya.
claims.quote: the first-born, the giant Xelhua, of Itzocan and Epatlan, and Cuauquechollan, the cities he founded.

claims.statement: The passage quoted in the article says that in the first age there were giants in this country, whom they called tzocuilicxe.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan yang dimuat artikel itu disebutkan bahwa pada zaman pertama ada raksasa di negeri ini yang disebut tzocuilicxe.
claims.quote: Hubo, en esta primera edad, gigantes en este país, a los que llamaron tzocuilicxe

claims.statement: According to the legend, only seven brothers were saved in the caves of the mountain of Tlalocan.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda itu, hanya tujuh bersaudara yang selamat di gua-gua gunung Tlalocan.
claims.quote: solo siete hermanos se salvaron en las grutas de la montaña del Tlalocan.

claims.statement: According to the founding legend on a commemorative plaque, Xelhua the giant went to the place later called Cholollan, with great adobes made in Tlalmanalco and passed from hand to hand by a line of men.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda pendirian pada sebuah plakat peringatan, Xelhua si raksasa pergi ke tempat yang kemudian disebut Cholollan, dengan bata besar buatan Tlalmanalco yang dioper dari tangan ke tangan oleh barisan orang.
claims.quote: Xelhua, el gigante, fue al sitio que después se le llamó Cholollan y con grandes adobes fabricados en Tlalmanalco y conducidos de mano en mano por una fila de hombres

claims.statement: According to the legend, he began building the pyramid in memory of the mountain where he was saved; Tonacatecutli, father of all the gods, angered that the work threatened to reach the clouds, hurled celestial fire and a toad-shaped stone that killed many of the builders.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda itu, ia mulai membangun piramida untuk mengenang gunung tempat ia diselamatkan; Tonacatecutli, bapa semua dewa, marah karena bangunan itu mengancam mencapai awan, lalu melemparkan api langit dan batu berbentuk katak yang menewaskan banyak pembangun.
claims.quote: comenzó a construir la pirámide en memoria de la montaña en que fue salvado. Irritado Tonacatecutli, padre de todos los dioses, que la obra amenazaba con llegar a las nubes lanzó al fuego celeste y con una piedra en forma de sapo mató a muchos de los constructores

claims.statement: According to the legend, giants dwelt on the earth in the time of the flood and many perished submerged in the waters.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda itu, pada masa air bah raksasa-raksasa tinggal di bumi dan banyak yang tewas tenggelam.
claims.quote: en la época del diluvio moraban sobre la tierra los gigantes, muchos perecieron sumergidos en las aguas

claims.statement: According to the passage quoted in the article, one of the seven said to have escaped the flood went to Cholula and began building a tower; the captain's name was Xelua, and he built it to escape in it if the flood came again.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kutipan yang dimuat artikel itu, salah satu dari tujuh orang yang konon lolos dari air bah pergi ke Cholula dan mulai membangun sebuah menara; nama kapten itu Xelua, dan ia membangunnya agar dapat menyelamatkan diri bila air bah datang lagi.
claims.quote: Uno de aquellos siete, que dicen haber escapado del diluvio, dicen que multiplicándose [...] se fue a Cholula y ahí comenzó edificar una torre que es aquella de la cual ahora aparece la base de ladrillos. El nombre de este capitán era Xelua. La edificaba para, en caso de venir el diluvio otra vez, poder escapar en ella.

claims.statement: According to the passage, when the tower had reached a great height a lightning bolt fell from the sky and destroyed it, killing many people.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kutipan itu, ketika menara sudah sangat tinggi, petir jatuh dari langit, merusaknya, dan menewaskan banyak orang.
claims.quote: Y estando ya en gran altura, cayó del cielo un rayo y la destruyó matando mucha gente.

claims.statement: According to the passage from an early chronicle, Ilancueitl had six sons; the first was called Gelhua or Xelua, who settled Cuauhquechulan (Huaquechula), Itzucan (Izúcar), Tzepatlan (Epatlán) and Teopantlan.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kutipan dari sebuah kronik awal, Ilancueitl memiliki enam anak; yang pertama bernama Gelhua atau Xelua, yang mendirikan permukiman di Cuauhquechulan (Huaquechula), Itzucan (Izúcar), Tzepatlan (Epatlán), dan Teopantlan.
claims.quote: Este de su mujer llamada Ilancueitl hobo seis hijos. El primero llamaron Gelhua [...] o Xelua [...] este pobló a Cuauhquechulan (Huaquechula) y a Itzucan (Izúcar), Tzepatlan (Epatlán), Teopantlan

claims.statement: According to the article, Xelhuan is one of four Nonoalca rulers who migrated from Tula to the Puebla Valley in the early twelfth century.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel itu, Xelhuan adalah salah satu dari empat penguasa Nonoalca yang bermigrasi dari Tula ke Lembah Puebla pada awal abad ke-12.
claims.quote: Xelhuan es uno entre los cuatro gobernantes nonoalcas (Ueuetzin, Quauhtzin, Citlalmacuetzin son los otros), que emigraron desde Tula hacia el Valle de Puebla a principios del siglo XII.

claims.statement: According to the article, in the year 1 tecpal, that is 1116, Xelhua migrates with his people.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel itu, pada tahun 1 tecpal, yaitu 1116, Xelhua bermigrasi bersama rakyatnya.
claims.quote: en un año 1 tecpal, es decir, en 1116, Xelhua emigra con su pueblo

claims.statement: According to the article, no source says Xelhuan stopped in Cholula except the Códice Vaticano A, which places him as builder of the pyramid in Cholula in the "improbable" year 1194.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel itu, tidak ada sumber yang menyebut Xelhuan berhenti di Cholula kecuali Códice Vaticano A, yang menempatkannya sebagai pembangun piramida di Cholula pada tahun 1194 yang dinilai tidak mungkin.
claims.quote: según lo anotó Kirchhoff, ninguna fuente menciona que Xelhuan se detuvo en Cholula salvo el Códice Vaticano A, que lo ubica como constructor de la pirámide en Cholula en la improbable fecha de 1194.

claims.statement: According to the article's author, Xelhuan was not a "captain" as narrated by Veytia's legend on the plaque, still less the builder of the Cholula pyramid.
claims.statement_id: Menurut penulis artikel, Xelhuan bukan seorang "kapten" seperti dikisahkan legenda Veytia pada plakat itu, apalagi pembangun piramida Cholula.
claims.quote: Xelhuan no fue, entonces, un “capitán”, como narra la leyenda de Veytia en la placa “conmemorativa de su fundación” en Cholula, siguiendo el Códice Ríos; menos aún el constructor de la pirámide cholulteca

claims.statement: The article's author concludes that this Nonoalca Chichimeca warrior had a normal stature and was never in the great Cholollan.
claims.statement_id: Penulis artikel menyimpulkan bahwa prajurit Nonoalca Chichimeca ini bertubuh normal dan tidak pernah berada di Cholollan yang besar.
claims.quote: con seguridad este guerrero nonoalca chichimeca que la HTC dice murió en el camino, quien tuvo una estatura normal, nunca estuvo en la gran Cholollan.

claims.statement: According to the article, they all arrived at the beginning of the twelfth century in a city whose ceremonial center, its pyramid, had already stood for many centuries.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel itu, mereka semua tiba pada awal abad ke-12 di sebuah kota yang pusat upacaranya, yaitu piramidanya, sudah berabad-abad berdiri.
claims.quote: todos ellos llegaron, a comienzos del siglo XII, a una ciudad cuyo centro ceremonial, es decir su pirámide, llevaba ya muchos siglos de haberse erigido.

claims.statement: According to the article, the oral traditions of Cholula's neighborhoods keep attributing the founding of their city to an ancient "captain" and "giants".
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel itu, tradisi lisan lingkungan Cholula terus menisbahkan saat pendirian kota mereka kepada seorang "kapten" dan "raksasa" kuno.
claims.quote: En las tradiciones orales de los barrios de Cholula, sin embargo, ... se insiste en atribuirle a un “capitán” y a “gigantes” antiguos el momento de la fundación de su ciudad.

claims.statement: According to the article, in various neighborhoods of Cholula there are several versions about bones of giants, always described as belonging to "gentiles", that keep appearing.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel itu, di berbagai lingkungan Cholula ada beberapa versi tentang tulang raksasa, selalu digambarkan sebagai milik "kaum kafir", yang terus bermunculan.
claims.quote: En las tradiciones orales de los barrios de Cholula, sin embargo, ... existen varias versiones, en diversos barrios, sobre los huesos de gigantes, siempre descritos como de “gentiles”, que continúan apareciendo

claims.statement: Xelhua or Xelhuan was the name of a figure in Nahua origin stories interpreted as a mythical giant, prince or "deity", the son of Ilancueitl, active in the Tehuacan Valley.
claims.statement_id: Xelhua atau Xelhuan adalah nama tokoh dalam kisah asal-usul Nahua yang ditafsirkan sebagai raksasa mitos, pangeran, atau "dewa", putra Ilancueitl, yang aktif di Lembah Tehuacan.
claims.quote: Xelhua or Xelhuan was the name of a figure in Nahua origin stories who has been interpreted as a mythical giant, prince, or "deity," the son of Ilancueitl, and someone active in the Tehuacan Valley.

claims.statement: He may have climbed Mount Tlaloc to escape a flood, and some attribute to him the organizing of the huge pyramid's construction in Cholula.
claims.statement_id: Ia mungkin mendaki Gunung Tlaloc untuk lolos dari banjir, dan sebagian orang menganggapnya pengatur pembangunan piramida besar di Cholula.
claims.quote: He may have climbed Mount Tlaloc to escape a flood, and some attribute him with organizing the construction of the huge pyramid in Cholula.

claims.statement: In Inuit mythology, Aipaloovik is an evil sea god of death and destruction, the opposite of Anguta, and a danger to all fishermen.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Inuit, Aipaloovik adalah dewa laut jahat yang dikaitkan dengan kematian dan kehancuran, lawan Anguta, dan berbahaya bagi semua nelayan.
claims.quote: In Inuit mythology, Aipaloovik is an evil sea god associated with death and destruction. He is considered the opposite of Anguta. He is a danger to all fishermen.

claims.statement: The Inuit religion article lists Aipaloovik as an evil sea god associated with death and destruction.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Inuit religion mencantumkan Aipaloovik sebagai dewa laut jahat yang dikaitkan dengan kematian dan kehancuran.
claims.quote: Aipaloovik, an evil sea god associated with death and destruction

claims.statement: Aipaloovik appears in an incomplete list of Inuit deities believed to hold power over some specific part of the Inuit world.
claims.statement_id: Aipaloovik termasuk dalam daftar tidak lengkap dewa Inuit yang dipercaya berkuasa atas bagian tertentu dari dunia Inuit.
claims.quote: Below is an incomplete list of Inuit deities believed to hold power over some specific part of the Inuit world

claims.statement: Inuit religion is the traditional religion of certain circumpolar peoples, practised within Inuit communities in parts of Chukotka, Alaska, northern Canada, and Greenland.
claims.statement_id: Agama Inuit adalah agama tradisional bangsa-bangsa tertentu di sekitar kutub, dianut di komunitas Inuit di sebagian Chukotka, Alaska, Kanada utara, dan Greenland.
claims.quote: Inuit religion is the traditional religion of certain circumpolar peoples. It is practised within Inuit communities in parts of Chukotka, Alaska, northern Canada, and Greenland.

claims.statement: In the same list of Inuit deities, Anguta is the gatherer of the dead who carries them into the underworld, where they must sleep for a year.
claims.statement_id: Dalam daftar dewa Inuit yang sama, Anguta disebut pengumpul orang mati yang membawa mereka ke dunia bawah, tempat mereka harus tidur selama satu tahun.
claims.quote: Anguta: gatherer of the dead; he carries them into the underworld, where they must sleep for a year.

claims.statement: Anguta is a psychopomp who ferries souls from the land of the living to the underworld, called Adlivun, where his daughter rules.
claims.statement_id: Anguta adalah pengantar arwah yang membawa jiwa dari dunia orang hidup ke dunia bawah bernama Adlivun, tempat putrinya berkuasa.
claims.quote: Anguta is a psychopomp, ferrying souls from the land of the living to the underworld, called Adlivun, where his daughter rules.

claims.statement: Anguta is the father of the sea goddess Sedna in the Inuit religion.
claims.statement_id: Anguta adalah ayah dewi laut Sedna dalam agama Inuit.
claims.quote: is the father of the sea goddess Sedna in the Inuit religion.

claims.statement: Boiuna ("Black Snake") is a creature of Brazilian mythology, also called Cobra-Grande ("Large Serpent") and Mboiaçu.
claims.statement_id: Boiuna ("ular hitam") adalah makhluk mitologi Brasil, juga disebut Cobra-Grande ("ular besar") dan Mboiaçu.
claims.quote: Boiuna (translated as "Black Snake") is a mythological creature in Brazilian mythology. It is also known as the Cobra-Grande (translated as "Large Serpent") and the Mboiaçu.

claims.statement: The Boiuna is a nocturnal black snake, the most powerful creature of the Amazon rivers.
claims.statement_id: Boiuna adalah ular hitam yang aktif malam hari dan makhluk terkuat di sungai-sungai hutan Amazon.
claims.quote: The Boiuna is a nocturnal black snake creature which is the most powerful creature of the rivers within the Amazon rainforest.

claims.statement: It can become a canoe, a sailboat or a woman to frighten fishermen entering its territory.
claims.statement_id: Ia dapat berubah wujud menjadi kano, perahu layar, atau perempuan untuk menakuti nelayan yang memasuki wilayahnya.
claims.quote: It can take on various shapes in order to frighten away any fishermen that enter its territory. Some of the forms the Boiuna can take on are a canoe, a sailboat and a woman.

claims.statement: The Boiúna is a gigantic snake that lives at the bottom of the rivers, lakes and igarapés of the Amazon, in a place called "boiaçuquara" or "home of the great snake".
claims.statement_id: Boiúna adalah ular raksasa yang hidup di dasar sungai, danau, dan igarapé di Amazon, di tempat bernama "boiaçuquara" atau "rumah ular besar".
claims.quote: A Boiúna é uma cobra gigantesca que vive no fundo dos rios, lagos e igarapés da Amazônia, num lugar chamado “boiaçuquara” ou “morada da cobra grande”.

claims.statement: Its eyes radiate a powerful light that attracts fishermen who approach thinking it is a large boat; when they get close, they become its food.
claims.statement_id: Mata ular itu memancarkan cahaya kuat yang menarik nelayan yang mengira itu kapal besar; saat mendekat, mereka menjadi makanannya.
claims.quote: Seus olhos irradiam uma luz poderosa a qual atrai os pescadores que se aproximam pensando se tratar de um barco grande. Mas quando eles chegam perto dela, viram seu alimento.

claims.statement: The Boiúna can transform into the most disparate figures, such as ships, steamers and canoes, to deceive and swallow people.
claims.statement_id: Boiúna dapat berubah menjadi aneka rupa, seperti kapal, kapal uap, dan kano, untuk menipu dan menelan orang.
claims.quote: A Boiúna pode se transformar nas mais disparatadas figuras: navios, vapores, canoas… para enganar e engolir as pessoas.

claims.statement: Its legend belongs to the mythic cycle of "how night came about", in which the Cobra Grande marries off her daughter and sends her night shut inside a tucumã seed.
claims.statement_id: Legendanya bagian dari siklus mitos "bagaimana malam muncul": Cobra Grande menikahkan putrinya dan mengirimkan malam yang terkurung dalam biji tucumã.
claims.quote: Sua lenda faz parte do ciclo mítico de “como surgiu a noite”, segundo a qual a Cobra Grande casa a filha e manda-lhe a noite presa dentro de um caroço de tucumã.

claims.statement: In another legend, an indigenous woman pregnant by Boiúna gave birth to twin snake-children: a boy named Honorato (or Nonato) and a girl named Maria.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda lain, seorang perempuan pribumi yang mengandung anak Boiúna melahirkan sepasang anak-ular kembar: Honorato (atau Nonato) dan Maria.
claims.quote: uma índia, grávida de Boiúna (Cobra-grande, Sucuri), deu à luz duas crianças-cobras gêmeas: um menino, que recebeu o nome de Honorato (ou Nonato) e uma menina chamada Maria.

claims.statement: Ciência Hoje das Crianças calls Boiuna a very old Amazonian legend that arose among the indigenous peoples of the region.
claims.statement_id: Ciência Hoje das Crianças menyebut Boiuna sebagai legenda Amazon yang sangat tua, lahir di kalangan masyarakat pribumi di sana.
claims.quote: Boiuna é uma lenda amazônica muito antiga, que surgiu entre os indígenas da região.

claims.statement: According to the legend, the Boiuna lives at the bottom of the rivers, lakes and igarapés of the Amazon, a snake so huge it can swallow people and even whole boats.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, di dasar sungai, danau, dan igarapé Amazon hidup Boiuna, ular yang begitu besar sehingga mampu menelan orang dan bahkan seluruh perahu.
claims.quote: Reza a lenda que no fundo dos rios, lagos e igarapés da Amazônia vive a Boiuna – uma cobra tão grande, mas tão grande, que é capaz de engolir pessoas e até embarcações inteiras!

claims.statement: Some also say that the giant snake left descendants: Honorato and Maria Caninana.
claims.statement_id: Ada pula yang bercerita bahwa ular raksasa itu meninggalkan keturunan: Honorato dan Maria Caninana.
claims.quote: Há também quem espalhe que a cobra gigante deixou descendentes: Honorato e Maria Caninana.

claims.statement: In Aztec mythology, Chalchiuhtlatonal was a water god related to Chalchiuhtlicue who watches over the sea and protects its animals.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Aztek, Chalchiuhtlatonal adalah dewa air yang terkait dengan Chalchiuhtlicue; ia mengawasi laut dan melindungi hewan di dalamnya.
claims.quote: was a god of water, related to Chalchiuhtlicue. He looks over the sea, and protects the animals living in it.

claims.statement: The article on Chalchiuhtlicue says she belongs to a larger group of Aztec rain gods and is closely related to the water god Chalchiuhtlatonal.
claims.statement_id: Artikel tentang Chalchiuhtlicue menyebut dewi itu termasuk kelompok besar dewa hujan Aztek dan berkerabat dekat dengan dewa air Chalchiuhtlatonal.
claims.quote: Chalchiuhtlicue belongs to a larger group of Aztec rain gods, and she is closely related to the water god Chalchiuhtlatonal.

claims.statement: Chalchiuhtlicue is associated with fertility, and she is the patroness of childbirth.
claims.statement_id: Chalchiuhtlicue dikaitkan dengan kesuburan dan menjadi pelindung persalinan.
claims.quote: Chalchiuhtlicue is associated with fertility, and she is the patroness of childbirth.

claims.statement: Chalchiuhtlicue was highly revered at the time of the Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire and was an important deity for the Nahuas in the Postclassic period of central Mexico.
claims.statement_id: Chalchiuhtlicue sangat dihormati pada masa penaklukan Spanyol atas Kekaisaran Aztek dan merupakan dewi penting bagi bangsa Nahua pada periode Pascaklasik di Meksiko tengah.
claims.quote: Chalchiuhtlicue was highly revered at the time of the Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire, and she was an important deity for the Nahuas in the Postclassic period of central Mexico.

claims.statement: Depending on the text, Chalchiuhtlicue was the wife or sister of the Aztec rain god Tlaloc.
claims.statement_id: Menurut teks yang berbeda, Chalchiuhtlicue adalah istri atau saudari dewa hujan Aztek, Tlaloc.
claims.quote: Chalchiuitlicue was the wife or sister of the Aztec god of rain Tlaloc, depending on the text.

claims.statement: In Aztec religion, Chalchiuhtlicue helps Tlaloc rule the paradisial kingdom of Tlalocan.
claims.statement_id: Dalam agama Aztek, Chalchiuhtlicue membantu Tlaloc memerintah kerajaan surgawi Tlalocan.
claims.quote: In Aztec religion, Chalchiuitlicue helps Tlaloc to rule the paradisial kingdom of Tlalocan.

claims.statement: In American folklore, Chessie is a sea monster said to live in Chesapeake Bay.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Amerika, Chessie adalah monster laut yang konon hidup di Teluk Chesapeake.
claims.quote: In American folklore, Chessie is a sea monster said to live in the midst of the Chesapeake Bay.

claims.statement: Sighting claims appear in local media and regional books from 1936 on.
claims.statement_id: Klaim penampakannya muncul di media lokal dan buku-buku daerah sejak 1936.
claims.quote: Claims of sightings appear in local media and regionally-themed books from 1936 onward.

claims.statement: Over time Chessie became an environmental icon tied to the bay's ecological health.
claims.statement_id: Lambat laun Chessie menjadi ikon lingkungan yang dikaitkan dengan kesehatan ekologi Teluk Chesapeake.
claims.quote: Over time, the figure developed into an environmental icon. Chessie is associated with the ecological health of the Chesapeake Bay

claims.statement: Reports repeatedly describe Chessie as serpentine, about twenty-five to forty feet long and eight to ten inches in diameter, with an elliptical or football-shaped head.
claims.statement_id: Laporan menggambarkan Chessie berulang kali sebagai makhluk menyerupai ular, panjang sekitar dua puluh lima sampai empat puluh kaki, berdiameter delapan sampai sepuluh inci, dengan kepala berbentuk elips atau seperti bola football.
claims.quote: has been repeatedly described as serpentine, about twenty-five to forty feet in length, eight to ten inches in diameter, and possessing an elliptical or football-shaped head.

claims.statement: According to the page author, Chessie's notoriety only really surfaced in 1978, when Virginia newspapers began printing contemporary sightings.
claims.statement_id: Menurut penulis halaman itu, ketenaran Chessie baru benar-benar muncul pada 1978, ketika surat kabar Virginia mulai memuat laporan penampakan terkini.
claims.quote: Chessie's notoriety really surfaced as recently as 1978 when Virginia newspapers began printing contemporary sightings of the beast.

claims.statement: On May 31, 1982, Maryland resident Robert Frew videotaped a long, dark, serpent-like creature swimming in Chesapeake Bay about 100 feet off the bulkhead of his Kent Island home.
claims.statement_id: Pada 31 Mei 1982, Robert Frew, warga Maryland, merekam video makhluk panjang, gelap, menyerupai ular yang berenang di Teluk Chesapeake sekitar 100 kaki dari dermaga rumahnya di Kent Island.
claims.quote: until May 31, 1982. On that date around 7:30 PM, Maryland resident Robert Frew videotaped a long, dark, serpent-like creature swimming in the Chesapeake Bay, about 100 feet off the bulkhead of his Kent Island home.

claims.statement: Scientists at the Smithsonian's Museum of Natural History, including Dr. George Zug, examined the Frew videotape and, although intrigued, could reach no conclusions.
claims.statement_id: Ilmuwan Smithsonian, termasuk Dr. George Zug, memeriksa video Frew dan, meski tertarik, tidak dapat menarik kesimpulan apa pun tentang objek di dalamnya.
claims.quote: an audience with Dr. George Zug and other scientists at the Smithsonian Institution's Museum of Natural History. After thoroughly examining the tape the scientists, although intrigued by what it apparently depicted, were unable to reach any conclusions

claims.statement: The Wikipedia article judges a 1936 Chessie sighting from a helicopter unlikely, if not impossible, since the earliest Sikorsky helicopter flight was near Stratford, Connecticut in 1939.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Wikipedia menilai penampakan Chessie dari helikopter pada 1936 tampak tidak mungkin, karena penerbangan helikopter Sikorsky paling awal terjadi di dekat Stratford, Connecticut, pada 1939.
claims.quote: However, a Chessie sighting from a helicopter in 1936 seems unlikely, if not impossible, as the earliest Sikorsky helicopter flight was near Stratford, Connecticut in 1939.

claims.statement: A sketch of an unknown sea creature by boater Trudy Guthrie was published by the Evening Sun in September 1980 and was later identified as a manatee from Florida.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah sketsa makhluk laut tak dikenal karya pelaut Trudy Guthrie dimuat di Evening Sun pada September 1980 dan kemudian diidentifikasi sebagai manatee dari Florida.
claims.quote: A sketch of an unknown sea creature, drawn by boater Trudy Guthrie, was published by the Evening Sun in September 1980. It was later identified as a manatee from Florida.

claims.statement: As an environmental icon of Chesapeake Bay, Chessie was used by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service in its 1986 educational coloring book Chessie: A Chesapeake Bay Story.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai ikon lingkungan Teluk Chesapeake, Chessie dipakai Dinas Perikanan dan Margasatwa AS dalam buku mewarnai edukatif tahun 1986, Chessie: A Chesapeake Bay Story.
claims.quote: Chessie, as an environmental icon for the Chesapeake Bay, was used by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service for its educational coloring book in 1986, Chessie: A Chesapeake Bay Story.

claims.statement: The Chullachaki is a mythical forest creature of the Peruvian and Brazilian Amazon.
claims.statement_id: Chullachaki adalah makhluk hutan mitos dari rimba Amazon Peru dan Brasil.
claims.quote: is a mythical forest creature of the Peruvian and Brazilian Amazonian jungle.

claims.statement: He is short and ugly, with one leg shorter and one foot larger, backward-pointing or hoof-shaped.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan pendek dan buruk rupa, dengan satu kaki lebih pendek dan satu telapak lebih besar, terbalik, atau berbentuk kuku.
claims.quote: He is generally described as short and ugly, with one leg shorter than the other and one foot either larger than the other, pointed backward or in the form of a hoof.

claims.statement: He lures victims deep into the jungle disguised as a family member, a long-unseen loved one or a prey animal.
claims.statement_id: Ia menyamar sebagai anggota keluarga atau orang tercinta yang lama tak dijumpai, atau sebagai hewan buruan, untuk memikat korban ke dalam hutan.
claims.quote: He does this by taking the form of a family member or a loved one long not seen, or disguising himself as a prey animal.

claims.statement: According to this journal article, the Chullachaqui is a mythological being of the forest, a short duende (goblin-like being) with animal feet, and a protector of the forest.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel jurnal ini, Chullachaqui adalah makhluk mitologi penghuni hutan, berwujud duende (makhluk kerdil) pendek dengan kaki hewan, dan pelindung hutan.
claims.quote: Ser mitológico que habita la selva, tiene la característica física de un duende bajito con los pies de un animal, él es protector de la selva.
