claims.statement: Moñái is the third son of Tau and Kerana, one of the seven legendary monsters of Guarani mythology.
claims.statement_id: Moñái adalah putra ketiga Tau dan Kerana, salah satu dari tujuh monster legendaris mitologi Guarani.
claims.quote: is the third son of Tau and Kerana and one of the seven legendary monsters of Guarani mythology.

claims.statement: Because he dominates birds with his hypnotic antennae, he is called "the lord of the air".
claims.statement_id: Karena menguasai burung dengan kekuatan hipnotis antenanya, ia disebut "penguasa udara".
claims.quote: He can climb trees with ease and slide down to hunt the birds on whom he feeds and dominates with the hypnotic power of his antennas. Because of this he is called "the lord of the air".

claims.statement: Moñái likes to steal and hide his loot in a cave.
claims.statement_id: Moñái suka mencuri dan menyembunyikan hasil curiannya di gua.
claims.quote: Moñái is fond of stealing and hiding the products of his misdeeds in a cave.

claims.statement: His dominions are the open fields.
claims.statement_id: Wilayah kekuasaannya adalah ladang terbuka.
claims.quote: His dominions are the open fields.

claims.statement: His continuous robbing and raiding in the villages provoked great discord, as everyone accused each other of the thefts and mysterious "disappearances" of belongings.
claims.statement_id: Perampokan dan penjarahannya yang terus-menerus di desa-desa memicu perselisihan besar karena semua orang saling menuduh atas pencurian dan "hilangnya" barang secara misterius.
claims.quote: His continuous robbing and raiding in the villages provoked great discord among the people as they all accuse each other for the robberies and mysterious "disappearances" of their belongings.

claims.statement: Moñái left her in Teju Jagua's care and went to find his other brothers: Mbói Tu'i, Yasy Yateré, Kurupí, Luisón and Ao Ao.
claims.statement_id: Moñái menitipkannya pada Teju Jagua lalu pergi mencari saudara-saudaranya yang lain: Mbói Tu'i, Yasy Yateré, Kurupí, Luisón, dan Ao Ao.
claims.quote: Moñái left her in the care of Teju Jagua and left to search for the rest of his brothers: Mbói Tu'i, Yasy Yateré, Kurupí, Luisón, and Ao Ao.

claims.statement: The townspeople joined to end the misdeeds of Moñái and his brothers; the beautiful Porâsý offered herself for the mission.
claims.statement_id: Penduduk bersatu untuk mengakhiri kejahatan Moñái dan saudara-saudaranya; Porâsý yang cantik menawarkan diri menjalankan tugas itu.
claims.quote: The townspeople joined to put an end to Moñái's misdeeds and those of his brothers. The beautiful Porâsý offered herself to carry out this mission.

claims.statement: She convinced Moñái that she had fallen in love with him and that before their wedding she wanted to meet his brothers.
claims.statement_id: Ia meyakinkan Moñái bahwa ia jatuh cinta kepadanya dan bahwa sebelum pesta pernikahan ia ingin bertemu saudara-saudaranya.
claims.quote: She convinced Moñái that she had fallen in love with him and that before they celebrated their wedding she wanted to meet his brothers.

claims.statement: Knowing she was lost, she ordered the people to burn the cave even with her inside; this killed Porasy herself but also destroyed Tau and Kerana's cursed descendants, including Moñai.
claims.statement_id: Karena tahu dirinya tak tertolong, ia memerintahkan orang membakar gua walau ia masih di dalam; itu menewaskan Porasy sendiri, tetapi juga berhasil memusnahkan keturunan terkutuk Tau dan Kerana, termasuk Moñai.
claims.quote: Knowing that she was lost she ordered the people to burn the cave, even with her inside. While this killed Porasy herself, it also successfully destroyed Tau and Kerana's cursed descendants, including Moñai himself.

claims.statement: In return for Porâsý's sacrifice, the gods lifted her soul and changed it into a small but intense point of light.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai balasan atas pengorbanan Porâsý, para dewa mengangkat jiwanya dan mengubahnya menjadi titik cahaya kecil namun terang.
claims.quote: In return for the sacrifice of Porâsý, the gods lifted her soul and changed it into a small but intense point of light.

claims.statement: Moñái is the third son of Tau and Kerana; the Guaraní natives considered him lord of the fields, the earth and the winds.
claims.statement_id: Moñái adalah putra ketiga Tau dan Kerana; penduduk asli Guaraní menganggapnya penguasa ladang, tanah, dan angin.
claims.quote: MOÑÁI es el tercer hijo de TAU y KERANA, los nativos guaraníes le consideraban señor de los campos, de la tierra y de los vientos.

claims.statement: He was said to live in the deepest streams and swampy places; one of his hiding places was near Yaguarón and another in Lake Ypoá.
claims.statement_id: Konon ia tinggal di sungai-sungai terdalam dan tempat berawa; salah satu persembunyiannya dekat Yaguarón dan yang lain di Danau Ypoá.
claims.quote: Se cuenta que habitaba en los arroyos más profundos y en lugares pantanosos. Uno de sus escondederos estaba cerca de Yaguarón y otro en el Lago Ypoá.

claims.statement: Moñái is a horrible serpent of extraordinary size, with two spikes on its head and pointed teeth.
claims.statement_id: Moñái adalah ular mengerikan berukuran luar biasa, dengan dua duri di kepala dan gigi runcing.
claims.quote: MOÑÁI es una horrible serpiente de dimensión extraordinaria, tiene en la cabeza dos púas y dientes puntiagudos.

claims.statement: Many scholars of Guaraní mythology affirm that Moñái is not a serpent that devours animals and humans, but rather a protector of wild animals, the winds and the birds.
claims.statement_id: Banyak peneliti mitologi Guaraní menyatakan Moñái bukan ular pemangsa hewan dan manusia, melainkan pelindung hewan liar, angin, dan burung.
claims.quote: muchos estudiosos de la mitología guaraní afirman que MOÑÁI no es una serpiente devoradora de animales y de seres humanos, sino más bien es protectora de animales silvestres, de los vientos y de los pájaros.

claims.statement: Yet Moñái is also painted as a thief of crops, plunderer of harvests and raider of kitchens; he keeps part of his misdeeds as trophies on the highest hills and in grottoes, out of sight.
claims.statement_id: Namun Moñái juga digambarkan sebagai pencuri tanaman, penjarah panen, dan perampas dapur; sebagian hasil kejahatannya disimpan sebagai trofi di bukit tertinggi dan di gua-gua, jauh dari pandangan.
claims.quote: De todos modos, también pintan a MOÑÁI como un ladrón de cultivos, saqueador de cosechas y rapiñero de cocinas. En los cerros más altos guarda parte de sus fechorías como trofeos, y también en las grutas, lejos de vista.

claims.statement: Several areas of Paraguay bear the name Moñaikuare, since country people believe this monstrous snake had its burrow in those dreadful places.
claims.statement_id: Ada beberapa wilayah di Paraguay bernama Moñaikuare, karena orang desa percaya ular monster ini memiliki sarangnya di tempat-tempat mengerikan itu.
claims.quote: Existen varias zonas del Paraguay con la denominación de MOÑAIKUARE, pues la gente del campo cree que esta monstruosa víbora tenía su madriguera en esos lugares horripilantes.

claims.statement: A simbi is a Central African guardian spirit of water and nature in Bakongo religion and in diaspora traditions such as Hoodoo and Palo.
claims.statement_id: Simbi adalah roh penjaga air dan alam dari Afrika Tengah dalam agama tradisional Bakongo, juga dalam tradisi diaspora Afrika seperti Hoodoo dan Palo.
claims.quote: is a Central African guardian spirit of the water and nature in traditional Bakongo religion, as well as in African diaspora spiritual traditions, such as Hoodoo in the southern United States and Palo in Cuba.

claims.statement: Simbi have historically been identified with water people or mermaids, pottery, snakes, gourds and fire.
claims.statement_id: Simbi secara historis dikaitkan dengan manusia air atau putri duyung, tembikar, ular, labu, dan api.
claims.quote: Simbi have been historically identified with water people, or mermaids, pottery, snakes, gourds, and fire.

claims.statement: Simbi is also spelled Cymbee and Sim'bi, with the plural Bisimbi or Basimbi.
claims.statement_id: Simbi juga ditulis Cymbee dan Sim'bi, dengan bentuk jamak Bisimbi atau Basimbi.
claims.quote: A Simbi (also spelled Cymbee and Sim'bi, pl. Bisimbi or Basimbi)

claims.statement: Some believe the word simbi derives from simba, a Kikongo word meaning "to hold, keep, preserve".
claims.statement_id: Sebagian orang percaya kata simbi berasal dari simba, kata Kikongo yang berarti "memegang, menjaga, melestarikan".
claims.quote: Some believe the word simbi derives from simba, a Kikongo word that means "to hold, keep, preserve"

claims.statement: The word basimbi also translates to "guardians", with the phrase isimba ia nsi later becoming "guardians of the land".
claims.statement_id: Kata basimbi juga diterjemahkan sebagai "penjaga", dan frasa isimba ia nsi kemudian menjadi "penjaga tanah".
claims.quote: The word basimbi also translates to "guardians" with the phrase isimba ia nsi later becoming "guardians of the land."

claims.statement: The Bakongo traditionally believe that bisimbi are magical water spirits (in Kikongo: nkisi mia mamba) that can appear as a person, a snake, pottery, a calabash vine, or Kalûnga, a spark of fire.
claims.statement_id: Orang Bakongo secara tradisional percaya bahwa bisimbi adalah roh air gaib (dalam Kikongo: nkisi mia mamba) yang dapat tampil sebagai manusia, ular, tembikar, sulur labu, atau Kalûnga, percikan api.
claims.quote: The Bakongo people traditionally believe that bisimbi are magically water spirits (in kikongo: nkisi mia mamba) that can appear as a person, a snake, pottery, a calabash vine, or Kalûnga, a spark of fire

claims.statement: They are seen as guardians of nature and intermediaries who travel the Kalûnga Line between Ku Seke, the physical world of the living, and Ku Mpémba, the spiritual world of the ancestors.
claims.statement_id: Mereka dipandang sebagai penjaga alam dan perantara yang menempuh Garis Kalûnga antara Ku Seke, dunia fisik orang hidup, dan Ku Mpémba, dunia roh para leluhur.
claims.quote: They are seen as the guardians of nature and the intermediaries who travel the Kalûnga Line between Ku Seke, the physical world of the living, and Ku Mpémba, the spiritual world of the ancestors.

claims.statement: Bisimbi are also believed to be spiritual guides, using storytelling and oral tradition to connect the living with the ancestors and their history.
claims.statement_id: Bisimbi juga dipercaya sebagai pemandu spiritual yang memakai penuturan cerita dan tradisi lisan untuk menghubungkan orang hidup dengan leluhur dan sejarah mereka.
claims.quote: Bisimbi are also believed to be spiritual guides, using storytelling and oral tradition to connect the living to the ancestors and their history.

claims.statement: The belief that bisimbi "inhabit rocks, gullies, streams, and pools, and are able to influence the fertility and well-being of those living in the area" was brought to the United States by enslaved Bakongo and Mbundu peoples.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan bahwa bisimbi "mendiami batu, parit, sungai kecil, dan kolam, dan mampu memengaruhi kesuburan dan kesejahteraan penduduk sekitar" dibawa ke Amerika Serikat oleh orang Bakongo dan Mbundu yang diperbudak.
claims.quote: The belief that bisimbi "inhabit rocks, gullies, streams, and pools, and are able to influence the fertility and well-being of those living in the area" was translocated to the United States by enslaved Bakongo and Mbundu peoples.

claims.statement: At Pooshee plantation on the Santee Canal, Ruffin stated that a young enslaved boy went to a fountain for water late at night and was very frightened by a cymbee (Simbi water spirit) running around and around the fountain.
claims.statement_id: Di perkebunan Pooshee di Terusan Santee, Ruffin menyatakan seorang anak budak pergi ke mata air larut malam dan sangat ketakutan oleh seorang cymbee (roh air Simbi) yang berlari mengelilingi mata air itu.
claims.quote: At Pooshee plantation on the Santee Canal not too far from Woodboo, Ruffin stated that a young slave boy went to a fountain for water late at night and was very frightened by a cymbee (Simbi water spirit) who was running around and around the fountain.

claims.statement: The earliest known record of simbi spirits was made in the nineteenth century by Edmund Ruffin, a wealthy slaveholder from Virginia.
claims.statement_id: Catatan paling awal yang diketahui tentang roh simbi dibuat pada abad ke-19 oleh Edmund Ruffin, pemilik budak kaya dari Virginia.
claims.quote: The earliest known record of simbi spirits was recorded in the nineteenth century by Edmund Ruffin who was a wealthy slaveholder from Virginia

claims.statement: Part of the superstition was that it was bad luck for anyone who saw one to tell of the occurrence or refer to it.
claims.statement_id: Bagian dari takhayul itu ialah bahwa membawa sial bagi siapa pun yang melihatnya untuk menceritakan atau menyinggungnya.
claims.quote: Part of the superstition was that it was bad luck for anyone who saw one to tell of the occurrence, or refer to it

claims.statement: Another account from an enslaved man said simbi spirits have long hair.
claims.statement_id: Kesaksian lain dari seorang pria yang diperbudak menyatakan roh simbi berambut panjang.
claims.quote: Another occurrence from an enslaved man said simbi spirits have long hair.

claims.statement: In Black American folklore, the Gullah Geechee people of the Carolina Lowcountry have a children's story called Sukey and the Mermaid about a girl named Sukey meeting a mermaid named Mama Jo.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Amerika Hitam, orang Gullah Geechee di Carolina Lowcountry punya cerita anak berjudul Sukey and the Mermaid tentang gadis bernama Sukey yang bertemu putri duyung bernama Mama Jo.
claims.quote: In Black American folklore, the Gullah Geechee people in the Carolina Lowcountry have a children's story called Sukey and the Mermaid about a girl named Sukey meeting a mermaid named Mama Jo.

claims.statement: In the story Mama Jo helps and protects Sukey and supported her financially by giving her gold coins.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita itu, Mama Jo menolong dan melindungi Sukey serta mendukungnya secara finansial dengan memberinya koin emas.
claims.quote: Mama Jo in the story helps and protects Sukey and financially supported her by giving her gold coins.

claims.statement: According to the source, this story comes from the belief in Simbi spirits in Central Africa that came to the United States during the Atlantic slave trade.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sumber itu, cerita ini berasal dari kepercayaan pada roh Simbi di Afrika Tengah yang dibawa ke Amerika Serikat pada masa perdagangan budak Atlantik.
claims.quote: This story comes from the belief in Simbi spirits in Central Africa that came to the United States during the Atlantic slave trade.

claims.statement: In Africa, Simbi nature spirits protect and provide riches to their followers.
claims.statement_id: Di Afrika, roh alam Simbi melindungi dan memberi kekayaan kepada para pengikutnya.
claims.quote: In Africa, Simbi nature spirits protect and provide riches to their followers.

claims.statement: Though often called lwa, bisimbi such as Mami Wata, Nsimba and Nzuzi are still nlongo, or sacred, in traditional Haitian spirituality and culture.
claims.statement_id: Meski sering disebut lwa, bisimbi seperti Mami Wata, Nsimba, dan Nzuzi tetap nlongo, atau sakral, dalam spiritualitas dan budaya tradisional Haiti.
claims.quote: Though often referred to as lwa, bisimbi such as Mami Wata, Nsimba and Nzuzi are still nlongo, or sacred, in traditional Haitian spirituality and culture.

claims.statement: In the Afro-Cuban religion called Palo, bisimbi are called both Nkitas and Mpungus.
claims.statement_id: Dalam agama Afro-Kuba bernama Palo, bisimbi disebut Nkitas dan Mpungus.
claims.quote: In an Afro-Cuban religion called Palo, bisimbi are called both Nkitas and Mpungus

claims.statement: They are believed to be guardians of all of nature, including lakes, forests or mountains.
claims.statement_id: Mereka dipercaya sebagai penjaga seluruh alam, termasuk danau, hutan, atau gunung.
claims.quote: They are believed to be guardians of all of nature, including lakes, forests or mountains.

claims.statement: According to the review, the simbi inhabit the natural world, just as elements of the natural world such as rocks and springs compose the spiritual landscape.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ulasan itu, simbi mendiami dunia alam, sebagaimana unsur alam seperti batu dan mata air membentuk lanskap spiritual.
claims.quote: the simbi inhabit the natural world, just as elements of the natural world, such as rocks and springs, compose the spiritual landscape.

claims.statement: According to the review, sacred stories present varied understandings of nature spirits as powerful guardians of human livelihood, spiritual experts (banganga) transitioned to the land of the dead, initiators of migrations, primordial inhabitants of natural formations, facilitators of natural disasters and catalysts of illness.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ulasan itu, kisah-kisah suci menyajikan beragam pemahaman tentang roh alam: penjaga penghidupan manusia yang kuat, ahli spiritual (banganga) yang beralih ke alam orang mati, pemrakarsa migrasi, penghuni purba bentukan alam, penyebab bencana alam, dan pemicu penyakit.
claims.quote: Sacred stories present the varied understandings of nature spirits as powerful guardians of human livelihood, spiritual experts (banganga) transitioned to the land of the dead, initiators of migrations, primordial inhabitants of natural formations, facilitators of natural disasters, and catalysts of illness.

claims.statement: According to the review, as guardians of the landscape the simbi sanctioned and ensured the success of subsistence activities.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ulasan itu, sebagai penjaga lanskap, simbi merestui dan menjamin keberhasilan kegiatan mencari nafkah.
claims.quote: As the guardians of the landscape, the simbi sanctioned and ensured the success of subsistence activities.

claims.statement: According to the review, some continental Africans began to understand the simbi as executors of misfortune and sought to harness their powers through capture, while Lowcountry Africans used the simbi to construct a sense of place amid captivity and displacement.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ulasan itu, sebagian orang Afrika di benua itu mulai memahami simbi sebagai pelaksana kemalangan dan berusaha memanfaatkan kekuatannya lewat penangkapan, sedangkan orang Afrika di Lowcountry memakai simbi untuk membangun rasa tempat di tengah penawanan dan keterasingan.
claims.quote: While some continental Africans began to understand the simbi as executors of misfortune and sought to harness their powers through capture, Lowcountry Africans used the simbi to construct a sense of place amid captivity and displacement.

claims.statement: According to the review, the simbi's place in the space between the land of the living and the land of the dead enabled them to assume the social function of familial ancestors.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ulasan itu, tempat simbi di ruang antara alam orang hidup dan alam orang mati memungkinkan mereka mengambil fungsi sosial leluhur keluarga.
claims.quote: Yet the simbi's inhabitance of the space between the land of the living and the land of the dead enabled them to assume the social function of familial ancestors.

claims.statement: According to the review, the simbi, nkisi and nkita are all "spirits of place", spirits of similar function in different regions of West and West-Central Africa.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ulasan itu, simbi, nkisi, dan nkita semuanya "roh tempat", roh dengan fungsi serupa di wilayah berbeda di Afrika Barat dan Afrika Tengah-Barat.
claims.quote: The simbi, nkisi, and nkita are all "spirits of place"; they are spirits of similar function in different regions of West and West-Central Africa.

claims.statement: The underwater panther (Mishipeshu) is one of the most important mythical water beings of many Indigenous peoples of the Northeastern Woodlands and Great Lakes, especially the Anishinaabeg.
claims.statement_id: Underwater panther (Mishipeshu) adalah salah satu makhluk air mitos terpenting bagi banyak bangsa pribumi di hutan timur laut dan Great Lakes, terutama Anishinaabeg.
claims.quote: is one of the most important of several mythical water beings among many Indigenous peoples of the Northeastern Woodlands and Great Lakes region, particularly among the Anishinaabeg.

claims.statement: Mishipeshu means "the Great Lynx"; it has a giant cat's head and paws, scales, and dagger-like spikes along its back and tail.
claims.statement_id: Mishipeshu berarti "Lynx Besar"; ia berkepala dan bercakar kucing raksasa, bersisik, dengan duri tajam di punggung dan ekornya.
claims.quote: Mishipeshu translates into "the Great Lynx". It has the head and paws of a giant cat but is covered in scales and has dagger-like spikes running along its back and tail.

claims.statement: In death he used his arm bone as a drumstick and his scapula as a drum.
claims.statement_id: Setelah mati, ia memakai tulang lengannya sebagai pemukul dan tulang belikatnya sebagai gendang.
claims.quote: In death he would use his arm bone as a drum stick and his scapula as a drum.

claims.statement: He made music and danced a jig that made the ground shake until boats overturned.
claims.statement_id: Ia menciptakan musik dan menarikan jig yang membuat tanah berguncang hingga perahu terbalik.

claims.statement: In Inuit religion, Alignak is a lunar deity and god of weather, water, tides, eclipses and earthquakes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam agama Inuit, Alignak adalah dewa bulan sekaligus dewa cuaca, air, pasang surut, gerhana, dan gempa bumi.
claims.quote: In the Inuit religion, Alignak is a lunar deity and god of weather, water, tides, eclipses, and earthquakes.

claims.statement: According to Larousse, all Eskimos have a moon-god; in Alaska, where Sedna is unknown, he reigns in solitary state.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Larousse, semua orang Eskimo memiliki dewa bulan; di Alaska, tempat Sedna tidak dikenal, ia berkuasa sendirian.
claims.quote: All Eskimos have a moon-god, but in Alaska, where Sedna is unknown, he reigns in solitary state as

claims.statement: The moon-god directs natural phenomena (tides, storms, eclipses, earthquakes, falling snow) and has all game and wild fowl at his disposal.
claims.statement_id: Dewa bulan itu mengatur gejala alam: pasang surut, badai, gerhana, gempa bumi, dan salju yang turun, serta menguasai semua binatang buruan dan unggas liar.
claims.quote: He directs natural phenomena: tides, storms, eclipses, earthquakes, falling snow, and he also has at his disposition all game and wild fowl.

claims.statement: In the account of the moon-god, Alignak drops the suppliants' future prey into the jars of water they hold out if the water is clear.
claims.statement_id: Dalam uraian tentang dewa bulan itu, Alignak menjatuhkan calon mangsa ke dalam wadah air yang diulurkan para pemohon jika airnya jernih.
claims.quote: Into the jars of water ... held out to him by suppliants Alignak drops their future prey if the water is clear

claims.statement: The spirit of the moon is redoubtable and at times irascible, but shows no particular malevolence towards men.
claims.statement_id: Roh bulan itu menakutkan dan kadang mudah marah, tetapi tidak menunjukkan kebencian tertentu kepada manusia.
claims.quote: Although redoubtable and at times irascible, the spirit of the moon evinces no particular malevolence towards men.

claims.statement: The moon-god is admired as an exemplary huntsman whose gifts and luck people would like to share.
claims.statement_id: Dewa bulan dikagumi sebagai pemburu teladan yang karunia dan keberuntungannya ingin dimiliki orang.
claims.quote: He is admired as an exemplary huntsman, whose gifts and luck one would like to share.

claims.statement: The Iglulik Eskimos say he wards off Sedna's far more terrifying anger by inflicting moderate punishment upon himself.
claims.statement_id: Orang Iglulik mengatakan ia menangkal kemarahan Sedna yang jauh lebih menakutkan dengan menghukum dirinya sendiri secara ringan.
claims.quote: Iglulik Eskimos say that he wards off Sedna’s anger (the two coexist in this mythology), which is by far the more terrifying, by inflicting moderate punishment upon himself.

claims.statement: His sister, the sun-goddess, plays a much smaller part and is not greatly concerned with the affairs of men.
claims.statement_id: Saudara perempuannya, dewi matahari, berperan jauh lebih kecil dan tidak terlalu peduli pada urusan manusia.
claims.quote: His sister, the sun-goddess, plays a much smaller part and is not greatly concerned with the affairs of men.

claims.statement: The Lunar deity article includes "Igaluk/Alignak of the Inuit" among its examples of male lunar gods.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Lunar deity memasukkan "Igaluk/Alignak" dari bangsa Inuit ke dalam contoh dewa bulan laki-laki.
claims.quote: Male lunar gods are also common, such as Sin of the Mesopotamians, Turks and of the Egyptians (or the earlier Egyptian lunar deity Iah), Mani of the Germanic tribes, Tsukuyomi of the Japanese, Igaluk/Alignak of the Inuit

claims.statement: The Big Myth site describes Alignak as the god of the moon, storms, earthquakes and tides.
claims.statement_id: Situs The Big Myth menyebut Alignak sebagai dewa bulan, badai, gempa bumi, dan pasang surut.
claims.quote: was the god of the moon, storms, earthquakes and tides.

claims.statement: Inuit religion is the traditional religion of certain circumpolar peoples, practised within Inuit communities in parts of Chukotka, Alaska, northern Canada, and Greenland.
claims.statement_id: Agama Inuit adalah agama tradisional bangsa-bangsa tertentu di sekitar kutub, dianut di komunitas Inuit di sebagian Chukotka, Alaska, Kanada utara, dan Greenland.
claims.quote: Inuit religion is the traditional religion of certain circumpolar peoples. It is practised within Inuit communities in parts of Chukotka, Alaska, northern Canada, and Greenland.

claims.statement: The same site says the Inuit pantheon varies slightly depending on where the particular Inuit live.
claims.statement_id: Menurut situs yang sama, pantheon Inuit sedikit berbeda-beda bergantung pada tempat tinggal kelompok Inuit tertentu.
claims.quote: The Inuit Pantheon varies slightly, depending on where the particular Inuit live.

claims.statement: Traditional Inuit theology encompasses a range of deities and spirits inhabiting the Arctic and subarctic landscapes.
claims.statement_id: Teologi tradisional Inuit mencakup berbagai dewa dan roh yang mendiami lanskap Arktik dan subarktik.
claims.quote: Traditional Inuit theology encompasses a range of deities and spirits inhabiting the Arctic and subarctic landscapes.

claims.statement: An alux is a kind of sprite or spirit in the mythology of some Maya peoples of the Yucatán Peninsula, Belize and Guatemala.
claims.statement_id: Alux adalah sejenis peri atau roh dalam tradisi mitologi beberapa bangsa Maya dari Semenanjung Yucatán, Belize, dan Guatemala.
claims.quote: is a type of sprite or spirit in the mythological tradition of certain Maya peoples from the Yucatán Peninsula, Belize and Guatemala

claims.statement: Aluxob are imagined as knee-high miniature Maya people in traditional dress.
claims.statement_id: Aluxob dibayangkan kecil, hanya setinggi lutut, dan mirip orang Maya berpakaian tradisional dalam ukuran mini.
claims.quote: Aluxo'ob are conceived of as being small, only about knee-high, and in appearance resembling miniature traditionally dressed Maya people.

claims.statement: Tradition holds they are usually invisible but can take physical form to communicate with or frighten humans.
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi, aluxob biasanya tak terlihat tetapi dapat mewujud untuk berkomunikasi dengan atau menakuti manusia.
claims.quote: Tradition holds that aluxob are generally invisible but are able to assume physical form for purposes of communicating with and frightening humans

claims.statement: They are linked to forests, caves, stones and fields but can be lured elsewhere with offerings.
claims.statement_id: Mereka dikaitkan dengan hutan, gua, batu, dan ladang, tetapi dapat dibujuk pindah dengan persembahan.
claims.quote: They are generally associated with natural features such as forests, caves, stones, and fields but can also be enticed to move somewhere through offerings.

claims.statement: Some Maya believe aluxo'ob are called into being when a farmer builds a little house on his property, most often in a maize field (milpa).
claims.statement_id: Sebagian orang Maya percaya aluxo'ob hadir ketika seorang petani membangun rumah kecil di tanahnya, paling sering di ladang jagung (milpa).
claims.quote: Some Maya believe that the Aluxo'ob are called into being when a farmer builds a little house on his property, most often in a maize field (milpa).

claims.statement: For seven years the alux helps the corn grow, summons rain and patrols the fields at night, whistling to scare off predators or crop thieves; at the end of that time the farmer must close the windows and doors of the little house, sealing the alux inside.
claims.statement_id: Selama tujuh tahun alux membantu jagung tumbuh, mendatangkan hujan, dan meronda ladang pada malam hari sambil bersiul untuk mengusir pemangsa atau pencuri hasil panen; setelah itu petani harus menutup jendela dan pintu rumah kecil itu sehingga alux terkurung di dalamnya.
claims.quote: For seven years, the alux will help the corn grow, summon rain and patrol the fields at night, whistling to scare off predators or crop thieves. At the end of seven years, the farmer must close the windows and doors of the little house, sealing the alux inside.

claims.statement: If people refuse, the aluxo'ob often wreak havoc and spread illness; if their conditions are met, the alux is thought to protect a person from thieves or even bring good luck.
claims.statement_id: Jika orang menolak memberi persembahan, aluxo'ob sering membuat kekacauan dan menyebarkan penyakit; jika syaratnya dipenuhi, alux dipercaya melindungi orang dari pencuri atau bahkan membawa keberuntungan.
claims.quote: If they refuse, the aluxo'ob will often wreak havoc and spread illness. However, if their conditions are met, it is thought the alux will protect a person from thieves or even bring them good luck.

claims.statement: Some suspect that the Maya belief in aluxob developed through interactions with the Spanish or pirates during the 16th century.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian orang menduga kepercayaan Maya akan aluxob berkembang lewat interaksi dengan orang Spanyol atau bajak laut pada abad ke-16.
claims.quote: some suspect that the Maya's belief of aluxob developed through interactions with the Spanish or pirates during the 16th century

claims.statement: The Maya themselves would say the alux are the spirits of their ancestors, or of the land itself, dating from before contact with Western civilization.
claims.statement_id: Orang Maya sendiri mengatakan alux adalah roh leluhur mereka atau roh tanah itu sendiri, sejak sebelum bersentuhan dengan peradaban Barat.
claims.quote: the Maya themselves would claim that the alux are the spirits of their ancestors, or the spirits of the land itself, preceding contact with Western civilization

claims.statement: It is said that the alux is a clay doll that guards the farmer's field, scaring away thieves and joking with the people who pass by or stop to rest near where it lives.
claims.statement_id: Dikatakan bahwa alux adalah boneka tanah liat yang menjaga ladang petani, menakut-nakuti pencuri dan mengerjai orang yang lewat atau berhenti beristirahat di dekat tempat tinggalnya.
claims.quote: It is said that the alux is a clay doll that guards the farmer's field, scaring away thieves and making jokes to all the people who pass by or stop to rest near the place where he lives.

claims.statement: The alux is made of clay mixed with honey, molded into a little doll, and given a dog and a slingshot made of the same clay.
claims.statement_id: Alux dibuat dari tanah liat bercampur madu, dibentuk menjadi boneka kecil, dan dilengkapi dengan anjing serta ketapel dari tanah liat yang sama.
claims.quote: The alux is made of clay mixed with honey, molded into the shape of a little doll, and with the same clay provided with his dog and slingshot.

claims.statement: To give the alux life, the farmer offers a drink of saká thirteen times, in the middle of the cornfield where the alux is placed under a rock.
claims.statement_id: Untuk menghidupkan alux, petani mempersembahkan minuman saká sebanyak tiga belas kali di tengah ladang jagung, tempat alux diletakkan di bawah batu.
claims.quote: To give life to the alux, the farmer offers a drink of saká ... on thirteen occasions. The offering must be made in the middle of the cornfield, where the alux is placed under a rock.

claims.statement: If someone tries to rob the farm by jumping over the stone fence, the alux will hiss at him and throw stones.
claims.statement_id: Jika seseorang hendak mencuri hasil ladang dengan melompati pagar batu, alux akan mendesis dan melemparinya dengan batu.
claims.quote: Should someone want to rob the farm, intending to jump over the stone fence, the alux will hiss at him and throw stones.

claims.statement: When the farmer finishes working the land, he destroys the alux by smashing it to pieces against a rock.
claims.statement_id: Setelah petani selesai menggarap tanah, ia menghancurkan alux dengan membantingnya ke batu.
claims.quote: When the farmer finishes working the land, he destroys the alux, smashing it to pieces against a rock.

claims.statement: The clay alux has to be destroyed exactly at twelve noon, because at that moment the alux is asleep.
claims.statement_id: Boneka alux harus dihancurkan tepat pukul dua belas siang karena pada saat itu alux sedang tidur.
claims.quote: It has to be done exactly at twelve noon, because at that moment the alux is asleep.

claims.statement: It is also said that a person who is alone when seeing the alux can get sick if he talks about it right away.
claims.statement_id: Dikatakan pula bahwa orang yang sendirian ketika melihat alux dapat jatuh sakit jika langsung menceritakannya.
claims.quote: It is also said that the person who is alone when he sees the alux can get sick if he talks about it immediately.

claims.statement: The Maya author notes that in fact few farmers used the alux to guard their fields, and most do not know exactly what an alux is or what use it is on the farm.
claims.statement_id: Penulis Maya ini mencatat bahwa sebenarnya hanya sedikit petani yang memakai alux untuk menjaga ladang, dan kebanyakan tidak tahu persis apa itu alux atau gunanya di ladang.
claims.quote: Actually, few farmers used the alux to guard their fields. Most of them do not know exactly what an alux is or his usefulness on the farm.

claims.statement: The text about the alux was originally written in Yucatecan Maya, the most widely spoken indigenous language in Mexico.
claims.statement_id: Teks tentang alux ini semula ditulis dalam bahasa Maya Yucatan, bahasa pribumi yang paling banyak dituturkan di Meksiko.
claims.quote: This work was written originally in Yucatecan Maya, the most widely spoken indigenous language in Mexico.

claims.statement: The anchanchu is a legendary Andean vampire mainly from the Aymara region of Bolivia.
claims.statement_id: Anchanchu adalah vampir legendaris Andes yang terutama berasal dari wilayah Aymara di Bolivia.
claims.quote: is a legendary Andean vampire largely originating from the Aymara region of Bolivia.

claims.statement: It takes the form of a helpless old traveler, a rich gold-toothed Aymara woman, a seductive gringa or a monstrous animal.
claims.statement_id: Ia menyamar sebagai pelancong tua tak berdaya, perempuan Aymara kaya bergigi emas, perempuan asing yang memikat, atau hewan mengerikan.
claims.quote: It shapeshifts into the form of a helpless, elderly traveler, a rich Aymara woman with gold teeth, a seductive gringa, or a monstrous animal.

claims.statement: When a passerby offers help, it drinks their blood until they die.
claims.statement_id: Saat orang lewat menawarkan bantuan, anchanchu mengisap darahnya hingga ia mati.
claims.quote: When a passerby offers to help, the anchanchu victimizes them and drinks their blood, causing them to die of blood loss or disease.

claims.statement: In Peru the anchanchu is a dwarf-like duende called Muki, living underground and fond of gold.
claims.statement_id: Di Peru, anchanchu adalah duende mirip kurcaci bernama Muki yang tinggal di bawah tanah dan menyukai emas.
claims.quote: In Peru, the anchanchu is a duende, similar to a dwarf. Called Muki or Muqui, it lives underground and has a penchant for gold.

claims.statement: The anchanchu is the most feared evil being among the Aymara people because of its lethality.
claims.statement_id: Anchanchu adalah makhluk jahat yang paling ditakuti di kalangan bangsa Aymara karena sifatnya yang mematikan.
claims.quote: The anchanchu is the most feared evil being among the Aymara people due to its lethality.

claims.statement: Anchanchus take advantage of people's compassion to suck blood from their lips or heart.
claims.statement_id: Anchanchu memanfaatkan belas kasihan orang untuk mengisap darah dari bibir atau jantung mereka.
claims.quote: Anchanchus take advantage of peoples' compassion to suck blood from their lips or heart.

claims.statement: According to tradition, anchanchu victims must be treated quickly with the help of yatiris or amautas, who make an offering known as ch'iyara misa ("black table").
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi, korban anchanchu harus segera ditangani dengan bantuan yatiri atau amauta, yang membuat persembahan bernama ch'iyara misa ("meja hitam").
claims.quote: According to tradition, anchanchu victims must be treated quickly with the help of yatiris or amautas, who make an offering known as ch'iyara misa ("black table")

claims.statement: According to tradition, the anchanchu is the illegitimate brother of Ekeko (Iqiqu).
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi, anchanchu adalah saudara tidak sah dari Ekeko (Iqiqu).
claims.quote: According to tradition, the anchanchu is the illegitimate brother of Ekeko (Iqiqu)

claims.statement: While many popular online sources depict anchanchu as a demonic figure, Aymara mythology casts him as a gatekeeper of the underground mineral world, and homage must be paid to him before mining the Earth's resources.
claims.statement_id: Meskipun banyak sumber populer di internet menggambarkan anchanchu sebagai sosok iblis, mitologi Aymara menempatkannya sebagai penjaga gerbang dunia mineral bawah tanah, dan penghormatan harus diberikan kepadanya sebelum menambang sumber daya Bumi.
claims.quote: While many popular online sources depict anchanchu as a demonic figure, Aymara mythology casts him as a gatekeeper of the underground mineral world, and homage must be paid to anchanchu before mining the Earth's resources.

claims.statement: The anchanchu lives in the most desolate caves and grottoes of the altiplano, a plateau in the Andes Mountains.
claims.statement_id: Anchanchu tinggal di gua dan relung paling sunyi di altiplano, dataran tinggi di Pegunungan Andes.
claims.quote: The anchanchu lives in the most desolate caves and grottoes of the altiplano, a plateau in the Andes Mountains.

claims.quote: que mora en las cuevas, en el fondo de los ríos y en edificios ruinosos y abandonados

claims.statement: Paredes writes that the Anchanchu draws in his victims with his flattering courtesies and welcomes them gladly.
claims.statement_id: Paredes menulis bahwa Anchanchu memikat korbannya dengan sikap manis yang berlebihan dan menyambut mereka dengan gembira.
claims.quote: El Anchanchu atrae a sus víctimas con sus salamerías, y las recibe regocijado y

claims.statement: Paredes calls the Anchanchu a sinister deity who always smiles and, smiling, prepares and causes the greatest harm.
claims.statement_id: Paredes menyebut Anchanchu sebagai dewa yang sinister, yang selalu tersenyum dan sambil tersenyum menyiapkan serta menimbulkan kerusakan terbesar.
claims.quote: El Anchanchu es una deidad siniestra, que sonríe siempre y sonriendo prepara y causa los mayores daños

claims.statement: According to Paredes, when it travels along the roads it produces hurricanes and whirlwinds.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Paredes, ketika berjalan di jalan ia menimbulkan angin kencang dan pusaran angin.
claims.quote: Cuando transita por los caminos, produce huracanes y remolinos de viento

claims.statement: Paredes records that people rarely dare to spend the night (pernoctar) near rivers or in uninhabited houses (casas deshabitadas), out of fear of this terrible deity whose name they avoid even pronouncing.
claims.statement_id: Paredes mencatat bahwa orang Aymara jarang berani bermalam di dekat sungai atau di rumah kosong, karena takut pada dewa yang mengerikan ini, yang namanya pun enggan diucapkan.
claims.quote: rara vez se atreve a pernoctar cerca a los ríos o en casas deshabitadas ... terrible deidad, cuyo nombre excusa aún pronunciarlo

claims.statement: The Bolivian Catholic University glossary calls Anchanchu a relatively negative force that dwells in river bottoms, in mountain caves and crevices, in ravines, underground in desolate places, and in uninhabited houses.
claims.statement_id: Glosarium Universitas Katolik Bolivia menyebut Anchanchu sebagai kekuatan yang relatif negatif yang tinggal di dasar sungai, gua dan celah gunung, jurang, bawah tanah di tempat sunyi, dan rumah kosong.
claims.quote: Una fuerza relativamente negativa que mora en los fondos de los ríos, en las cuevas y grietas de las montañas, en las quebradas, bajo tierra en lugares desolados y en casas deshabitadas.

claims.statement: Ao Ao is a monstrous creature of South American mythology, one of the cursed sons of Tau and Kerana in Guarani-speaking cultures.
claims.statement_id: Ao Ao adalah makhluk mengerikan dari mitologi Amerika Selatan, salah satu putra terkutuk Tau dan Kerana dalam budaya berbahasa Guarani.
claims.quote: Ao Ao is the name of a monstrous creature from South American mythology. As one of the cursed sons of Tau and Kerana, it is one of the central mythological creatures among Guarani-speaking cultures.

claims.statement: It is often a voracious sheep-like creature with huge fangs.
claims.statement_id: Ao Ao sering digambarkan sebagai makhluk rakus mirip domba dengan taring besar.
claims.quote: The Ao Ao is often described as being a voracious sheep-like creature with a massive set of fangs.

claims.statement: Its name comes from its howl, "Ao ao ao!", when chasing victims.
claims.statement_id: Namanya berasal dari lolongan "Ao ao ao!" saat memburu korbannya.
claims.quote: Its name is derived from the sound that it makes, howling "Ao ao ao!" when it is pursuing its victims.

claims.statement: Ao Ao is alternatively also described as a large, carnivorous peccary.
claims.statement_id: Ao Ao juga digambarkan sebagai pekari besar pemakan daging.
claims.quote: Alternatively, it is also described as being a large, carnivorous peccary.

claims.statement: Ao Ao is said to have people as its sole source of food.
claims.statement_id: Ao Ao dikatakan hanya makan manusia.
claims.quote: Ao Ao is said to have people as its sole source of food.

claims.statement: In some versions of the myth, Ao Ao feasts upon disobedient children brought to it by his brother, Jasy Jatere.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian versi mitos, Ao Ao menyantap anak-anak yang tidak patuh yang dibawakan oleh saudaranya, Jasy Jatere.
claims.quote: In some versions of the myth, the Ao Ao would feast upon disobedient children brought to it by his brother, Jasy Jatere.

claims.statement: In Paraguay, adults scare children by saying that Ao Ao will come after them.
claims.statement_id: Di Paraguay, orang dewasa menakut-nakuti anak-anak dengan mengatakan bahwa Ao Ao akan datang mengejar mereka.
