claims.statement: The Beast of Busco is a legendary Indiana creature described as an unusually large snapping turtle.
claims.statement_id: Beast of Busco adalah makhluk legenda Indiana yang digambarkan sebagai kura-kura penggigit yang luar biasa besar.
claims.quote: The Beast of Busco is a legendary creature in Indiana folklore, described as an unusually large snapping turtle.

claims.statement: Residents reported it near Churubusco, Indiana, in 1949, prompting a month-long search with national attention.
claims.statement_id: Warga melaporkan melihatnya dekat Churubusco, Indiana, pada tahun 1949, memicu pencarian sebulan yang menarik perhatian nasional.
claims.quote: It was reportedly sighted by local residents near Churubusco, Indiana, in 1949, prompting a month-long search that attracted national attention.

claims.statement: Despite great efforts, no conclusive evidence was found.
claims.statement_id: Meski dicari habis-habisan, tidak ada bukti pasti keberadaannya.
claims.quote: Despite extensive efforts to locate the animal, no conclusive evidence of its existence was found.

claims.statement: A farmer named Oscar Fulk said he spotted a massive turtle in a seven-acre lake on his northern Indiana property in 1898.
claims.statement_id: Seorang petani bernama Oscar Fulk mengaku pada 1898 melihat kura-kura raksasa di danau seluas tujuh acre di tanahnya di Indiana utara.
claims.quote: A farmer named Oscar Fulk spotted it in a seven-acre lake on his northern Indiana property in 1898: a massive turtle, Fulk swore, the size of a small dinosaur.

claims.statement: In July 1948, Ora Blue and Charley Wilson, fishing in the same lake, reported seeing a giant turtle gliding across the water's surface.
claims.statement_id: Pada Juli 1948, Ora Blue dan Charley Wilson yang sedang memancing di danau yang sama melaporkan melihat kura-kura raksasa meluncur di permukaan air.
claims.quote: In July 1948, two men, Ora Blue and Charley Wilson, were fishing in the same lake when they saw an implausibly giant turtle gliding across the water's surface.

claims.statement: They estimated the turtle weighed over 500 pounds and told Gale Harris, who now owned the lake and surrounding farmland.
claims.statement_id: Mereka memperkirakan berat kura-kura itu lebih dari 500 pon dan melapor kepada Gale Harris, pemilik danau dan lahan di sekitarnya.
claims.quote: They estimated the turtle must have weighed over 500 pounds and went off to tell Gale Harris, who now owned the lake and the farmland around it.

claims.statement: Harris tried various ways to trap the turtle, including sending in divers and draining the lake; all failed and nearly bankrupted him.
claims.statement_id: Harris mencoba berbagai cara menangkap kura-kura itu, termasuk menurunkan penyelam dan menguras danau; semuanya gagal dan nyaris membuatnya bangkrut.
claims.quote: He conceived and executed a variety of colorful attempts at trapping the turtle, sending in divers and even draining the lake. Each gambit failed, and together they almost led to his bankruptcy.

claims.statement: Some believe it was mistaken identity, plausibly an alligator snapping turtle, the largest freshwater turtle species on the continent.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian orang berpendapat itu salah identifikasi, kemungkinan kura-kura buaya (alligator snapping turtle), kura-kura air tawar terbesar di benua itu.
claims.quote: Some believe the turtle was a case of mistaken identity; specifically, it could plausibly have been an alligator snapping turtle, the largest species of freshwater turtle on the continent

claims.statement: The most likely explanation is that the real Beast of Busco was a spiny soft-shell turtle or a common snapping turtle.
claims.statement_id: Penjelasan yang tampaknya paling mungkin adalah bahwa Beast of Busco sebenarnya kura-kura lunak berduri atau kura-kura buas biasa (common snapping turtle).
claims.quote: What seems most likely—if less thrillingly monstrous—is that the real Beast of Busco was a spiny soft-shell turtle, or even a common snapping turtle.

claims.statement: Churubusco, now known as Turtle Town, USA, commemorates the Beast of Busco (now affectionately called Oscar) each June at Turtle Days.
claims.statement_id: Churubusco, yang kini dijuluki Turtle Town, USA, memperingati Beast of Busco (kini dipanggil akrab Oscar) setiap Juni dalam festival Turtle Days.
claims.quote: Churubusco, now known as Turtle Town, USA, has taken that lesson to heart. Each June, locals and tourists gather to commemorate the Beast of Busco—now affectionately called Oscar, possibly after the first man to own the lake—at Turtle Days

claims.statement: In 1948 Harris did eventually capture one turtle from the lake; it weighed just 14 pounds.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1948 Harris akhirnya menangkap satu kura-kura dari danau itu, beratnya hanya 14 pon.
claims.quote: Back in 1948, he did eventually capture one turtle from the lake. It weighed all of 14 pounds.

claims.statement: Life Magazine photographer Mike Shea visited the site and took 299 photographs, but the images were deemed unusable.
claims.statement_id: Fotografer Life Magazine, Mike Shea, mengunjungi lokasi dan mengambil 299 foto, tetapi hasilnya akhirnya dinilai tidak dapat dipakai.
claims.quote: Life Magazine photographer Mike Shea visited the site and took 299 photographs, but the images were ultimately deemed unusable.

claims.statement: In early 1949, a UPI reporter from Fort Wayne sent the story over the wire services, bringing the turtle to national attention.
claims.statement_id: Pada awal 1949, seorang wartawan UPI dari Fort Wayne mengirim cerita itu lewat kantor berita sehingga kura-kura tersebut menjadi perhatian nasional.
claims.quote: In early 1949, a UPI reporter from Fort Wayne transmitted the story through the wire services, bringing the turtle to national attention.

claims.statement: Eight months later, national newspapers picked up the story and the turtle gained its epithet, the "Beast of Busco".
claims.statement_id: Delapan bulan kemudian surat kabar nasional mengangkat cerita itu, dan kura-kura tersebut mendapat julukan "Beast of Busco".
claims.quote: Eight months later, national newspapers finally picked up the story, and the turtle gained its epithet, the “Beast of Busco.”

claims.statement: In northeastern Ohio and Michigan folklore, Bessie is a Lake Erie monster, also called South Bay Bessie or The Lake Erie Monster.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Ohio timur laut dan Michigan, Bessie adalah monster Danau Erie, juga disebut South Bay Bessie atau The Lake Erie Monster.
claims.quote: In northeastern Ohio and Michigan folklore, Bessie is a name given to a lake monster in Lake Erie, also known as South Bay Bessie or simply The Lake Erie Monster.

claims.statement: The first recorded sighting was in 1817.
claims.statement_id: Penampakan Bessie pertama yang tercatat terjadi pada tahun 1817.
claims.quote: The first recorded sighting of Bessie occurred in 1817

claims.statement: Bessie is reported as snake-like, 30 to 40 ft long and greyish.
claims.statement_id: Bessie dilaporkan mirip ular, panjang 30 hingga 40 kaki, dan berwarna keabuan.
claims.quote: Bessie is reported to be snake-like and 30 to 40 ft (9.1 to 12.2 m) long, at least a foot in diameter, with a grayish color.

claims.statement: Monster sightings have been reported on Lake Erie as far back as 1793, all over the lake from Fort Erie, Ontario, to Toledo, Ohio.
claims.statement_id: Penampakan monster di Danau Erie dilaporkan sejak 1793, tersebar di seluruh danau dari Fort Erie, Ontario, hingga Toledo, Ohio.
claims.quote: Monster sightings have been reported on Lake Erie as far back as 1793. The sightings reportedly took place all over the lake from Fort Erie, Ontario, to Toledo Ohio.

claims.statement: According to Rafinesque as quoted by Oudemans, on 3 July 1817 the crew of a schooner saw in Lake Erie, three miles from land, a creature 35 or 40 feet long and one foot in diameter, dark mahogany and nearly black.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kutipan Rafinesque dalam buku Oudemans, pada 3 Juli 1817 awak sebuah kapal layar melihat di Danau Erie, tiga mil dari daratan, makhluk sepanjang 35 atau 40 kaki, berdiameter satu kaki, berwarna mahoni gelap hampir hitam.
claims.quote: On the 3d. of July, 1817, one was seen in Lake Erie, three miles from land, by the crew of a schooner, which was 35 or 40 feet long, and one foot in diameter; its colour was a dark mahogany, nearly black.

claims.statement: An addition quoted from Rafinesque describes the Lake Erie water-snake as copper-coloured, bright-eyed and 60 feet long, with balls fired at a short distance having no effect on it.
claims.statement_id: Laporan tambahan dalam kutipan Rafinesque menyebut ular air Danau Erie berwarna tembaga, bermata terang, sepanjang 60 kaki, dan peluru dari jarak dekat tidak berpengaruh padanya.
claims.quote: described to be of a copper colour, with bright eyes, and 60 feet long. It is added, that at a short distance balls had no effect on him

claims.statement: Rafinesque was inclined to think the creature was a fish, possibly a gigantic species of eel.
claims.statement_id: Rafinesque cenderung menyimpulkan makhluk itu ikan, mungkin spesies belut raksasa.
claims.quote: I am inclined to believe it was a fish, until otherwise convinced: it might be a gigantic species of eel

claims.statement: Oudemans judged that Rafinesque had been the dupe of a hoax.
claims.statement_id: Oudemans menilai Rafinesque telah tertipu oleh lelucon.
claims.quote: Every one feels that Mr. Rafinesque was the dupe of a hoax

claims.statement: In a third 1817 incident near Toledo, two French settlers, the Dusseau brothers, met a huge monster on the beach, writhing in what they took to be its death throes.
claims.statement_id: Pada insiden ketiga tahun 1817 dekat Toledo, dua bersaudara Dusseau, pemukim Prancis, menjumpai makhluk raksasa di pantai yang menggeliat seperti sekarat.
claims.quote: A third 1817 incident took place near Toledo, when French settlers—two brothers named Dusseau—encountered a huge monster on the beach, writhing in what they took to be its death throes.

claims.statement: The brothers described it as shaped like a large sturgeon, except that it had arms.
claims.statement_id: Kedua bersaudara itu menggambarkannya berbentuk seperti ikan sturgeon besar, tetapi memiliki lengan.
claims.quote: shaped like a large sturgeon, except that it had arms

claims.statement: In July 1892 the entire crew of a ship bound from Buffalo, New York, to Toledo, Ohio, reported an extraordinary sighting carried by local newspapers.
claims.statement_id: Pada Juli 1892, seluruh awak kapal dari Buffalo, New York, menuju Toledo, Ohio, melaporkan penampakan luar biasa yang dimuat surat kabar setempat.
claims.quote: An extraordinary sighting which was carried by local newspapers took place by the entire crew of a ship bound from Buffalo, New York, to Toledo, Ohio, in July 1892.

claims.statement: The Conneaut Arts Center hosts the Lake Erie Monster Festival, which celebrates the legend of Lake Erie monsters.
claims.statement_id: Conneaut Arts Center menyelenggarakan Lake Erie Monster Festival yang merayakan legenda monster Danau Erie.
claims.quote: The center has been hosting the Lake Erie Monster Festival for the past six years. The festival celebrates the legend of Lake Erie monsters.

claims.statement: The cadejo is a supernatural spirit of Central American folklore of indigenous origin, a dog-like creature with blue eyes when calm and red when hostile.
claims.statement_id: Cadejo adalah roh gaib dari cerita rakyat Amerika Tengah berasal pribumi, digambarkan seperti anjing bermata biru saat tenang dan merah saat bermusuhan.
claims.quote: is a supernatural spirit in Central American folklore of indigenous origin. It is commonly depicted as a dog-like creature with blue eyes when calm and red eyes when hostile.

claims.statement: Legend says it wanders lonely roads at night.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, ia berkeliaran di jalan-jalan sepi pada malam hari.
claims.quote: According to legend, it wanders along isolated roads at night.

claims.statement: The white cadejo protects travelers, while the black cadejo tries to kill them.
claims.statement_id: Cadejo putih melindungi pelancong dari bahaya, sedangkan cadejo hitam berusaha membunuh mereka.
claims.quote: The white cadejo protects travelers from harm and danger, while the black cadejo attempts to kill them

claims.statement: In Costa Rica and Panama the cadejo is instead described as a single black creature that, despite its monstrous look, is generally considered harmless.
claims.statement_id: Di Kosta Rika dan Panama, cadejo justru digambarkan sebagai satu makhluk hitam yang, meski tampak menyeramkan, umumnya dianggap tidak berbahaya.
claims.quote: In Costa Rica and Panama, the cadejo is instead described as a single black creature that, despite its monstrous appearance, is generally considered harmless.

claims.statement: Guatemalan and Salvadoran folklore also tells of a cadejo that protects drunk people from those who wish to rob or harm them.
claims.statement_id: Cerita rakyat Guatemala dan El Salvador juga mengenal cadejo yang melindungi orang mabuk dari mereka yang hendak merampok atau mencelakai.
claims.quote: Guatemalan and Salvadoran folklore also tells of a cadejo that protects drunk people from those who wish to rob or harm them.

claims.statement: It is said that turning one's back on the cadejo or speaking to it can cause insanity.
claims.statement_id: Konon membelakangi cadejo atau berbicara kepadanya dapat membuat orang gila.
claims.quote: It is said that turning one's back on the cadejo or speaking to it can cause insanity.

claims.statement: The term cadejo is of Spanish origin, but the creature's mythological roots are mainly associated with Maya mythology and the shamanistic traditions of the Nahua peoples of Mesoamerica.
claims.statement_id: Istilah cadejo berasal dari bahasa Spanyol, tetapi akar mitologis makhluk ini terutama dikaitkan dengan mitologi Maya dan tradisi syamanistik bangsa Nahua di Mesoamerika.
claims.quote: Although the term cadejo is of Spanish origin, the mythological roots of the creature are primarily associated with Maya mythology and the shamanistic traditions of the Nahua peoples of Mesoamerica.

claims.statement: In Honduras it is said that to repel the black cadejo one should recite phrases such as "it smells of holiness" and "it smells of incense".
claims.statement_id: Di Honduras, konon untuk mengusir cadejo hitam orang mengucapkan frasa seperti "baunya kesucian" dan "baunya dupa".
claims.quote: In Honduras, it is said that to repel the black cadejo one should recite phrases such as "it smells of holiness", "it smells of incense"

claims.statement: In the Yucatán Peninsula it is described as a being "half dog, half man", possibly a ghostly anthropomorph (Winik Peek', in Yucatec Maya).
claims.statement_id: Di Semenanjung Yucatán, makhluk ini digambarkan "setengah anjing, setengah manusia", mungkin semacam hantu berwujud manusia (Winik Peek', dalam bahasa Maya Yucatec).
claims.quote: in the Yucatán Peninsula, it is described as a being "half dog, half man", possibly a kind of ghostly anthropomorph (Winik Peek’, in Yucatec Maya).

claims.statement: In Costa Rica and Nicaragua the creature is also known as el cadejos.
claims.statement_id: Di Kosta Rika dan Nikaragua, makhluk ini juga dikenal sebagai el cadejos.
claims.quote: In Costa Rica and Nicaragua, the creature is also known as el cadejos.

claims.statement: In Miguel Ángel Asturias's "Leyenda del Cadejo", the Cadejo appears on the meadows, steals girls with long braids and ties knots in horses' manes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam "Leyenda del Cadejo" karya Miguel Ángel Asturias, Cadejo muncul di dataran dan mencuri gadis berkepang panjang serta membuat simpul pada surai kuda.
claims.quote: Y asoma por las vegas el Cadejo, que roba mozas de trenzas largas y hace ñudos en las crines de los caballos.

claims.statement: Asturias describes the Cadejo as a long animal, twice a ram at full moon and the size of a weeping willow at new moon, with goat hooves, rabbit ears and a bat face.
claims.statement_id: Asturias menggambarkan Cadejo sebagai hewan panjang, dua kali domba jantan saat bulan purnama dan sebesar pohon willow menangis saat bulan baru, berkuku kambing, bertelinga kelinci, dan berwajah kelelawar.
claims.quote: convertido en un animal largo —dos veces un carnero por luna llena, del tamaño de un sauce llorón por la luna nueva—, con cascos de cabro, orejas de conejo y cara de murciélago

claims.statement: In Asturias's literary version, the "hombre-adormidera" drags to hell the black braid of a novice who would become Madre Elvira de San Francisco, and "thus the Cadejo is born".
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi sastra Asturias, "hombre-adormidera" menyeret ke neraka kepang hitam seorang novis yang kelak menjadi Madre Elvira de San Francisco, dan "begitulah Cadejo lahir".
claims.quote: el hombre-adormidera arrastró al infierno la trenza negra de la novicia que con el tiempo sería madre Elvira de San Francisco —así nace el Cadejo—

claims.statement: On 18 April 1930 Asturias published his collection of stories Leyendas de Guatemala (Ediciones Oriente, Madrid).
claims.statement_id: Pada 18 April 1930 Asturias merilis kumpulan cerita Leyendas de Guatemala (Ediciones Oriente, Madrid).
claims.quote: El 18 de abril de 1930 Asturias dio a conocer su valiosa colección de cuentos Leyendas de Guatemala (Ediciones Oriente, Madrid)

claims.statement: According to the Instituto Cervantes article, the Cadejo looks like a dog but is not one.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel Instituto Cervantes, Cadejo tampak seperti anjing, tetapi bukan anjing.
claims.quote: Parece un perro, pero no lo es.

claims.statement: Oral tradition at first spoke of a single beast, but Guatemalans today swear there are two: the Black Cadejo and the White Cadejo.
claims.statement_id: Tradisi lisan mula-mula bercerita tentang satu binatang, tetapi orang Guatemala masa kini bersumpah ada dua: Cadejo Hitam dan Cadejo Putih.
claims.quote: al principio de una sola bestia, los guatemaltecos de hoy juran que son dos: el Cadejo Negro y el Cadejo Blanco.

claims.statement: Some assert that the White Cadejo even protects men from the attacks of the Black Cadejo.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian orang meyakini Cadejo Putih bahkan melindungi para pria dari serangan Cadejo Hitam.
claims.quote: Algunos aseguran que el Cadejo Blanco se dedica incluso a proteger de los ataques del Cadejo Negro a los hombres

claims.statement: The legend is described as a product of cultural syncretism and a remnant of the ancient belief that every person has an animal companion; the mythical animal is believed to be a person's spiritual counterpart, their fates closely linked.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini disebut hasil sinkretisme budaya dan sisa kepercayaan kuno bahwa setiap orang memiliki hewan pendamping; hewan mitos itu diyakini sebagai pasangan spiritual manusia, dengan nasib yang saling terkait.
claims.quote: The legend is therefore a product of cultural syncretism and a remnant of the ancient belief that every person possesses an animal companion. The mythical animal is believed to be a person's spiritual counterpart, with the fate of one closely linked to that of the other.

claims.statement: The chickcharney is a legendary creature of the folklore of Andros in the Bahamas.
claims.statement_id: Chickcharney adalah makhluk legenda dalam cerita rakyat Andros, Bahama.
claims.quote: The chickcharney is a type of legendary creature in the folklore of Andros in the Bahamas.

claims.statement: They are mischievous feathered creatures with red eyes, three toes per foot and long prehensile tails.
claims.statement_id: Mereka digambarkan sebagai makhluk berbulu jahil bermata merah, berjari tiga di tiap kaki, dan berekor panjang yang dapat mencengkeram.
claims.quote: They are described as mischievous feathered creatures with red eyes, three toes on each foot, and long prehensile tails.

claims.statement: They live in pine forests and curse or bless travelers depending on how they are treated.
claims.statement_id: Mereka tinggal di hutan pinus dan akan mengutuk atau memberkati pelancong tergantung cara diperlakukan.
claims.quote: They are believed to live in pine forests and will either curse or bless travelers depending on how they are treated.

claims.statement: Their heads are said to be able to turn all the way around.
claims.statement_id: Kepala mereka konon dapat berputar penuh.
claims.quote: Their heads are said to be able to turn all the way around.

claims.statement: Chickcharneys are described either as large owls or as feathered humanoid creatures that merely resemble owls; they allegedly build nests by tying pine treetops together.
claims.statement_id: Chickcharney digambarkan sebagai burung hantu besar atau makhluk berbulu mirip manusia yang sekadar menyerupai burung hantu; konon mereka membuat sarang dengan mengikat pucuk pohon pinus.
claims.quote: They are described either as large owls or as feathered humanoid creatures that merely resemble owls. They allegedly build nests by tying the tops of pine trees together.

claims.statement: According to legend, a young Neville Chamberlain worked on a sisal plantation in the Bahamas owned by his father Joseph Chamberlain; it failed financially because he angered chickcharnies by cutting down their trees.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, Neville Chamberlain muda bekerja di perkebunan sisal milik ayahnya, Joseph Chamberlain, di Bahama; perkebunan itu merugi karena ia membuat marah chickcharney dengan menebang pohon mereka.
claims.quote: According to legend, when he was around 20 years old, Neville Chamberlain worked on a sisal plantation in the Bahamas owned by his father Joseph Chamberlain. The story states that the plantation faced financial failure because Chamberlain angered some chickcharnies by cutting down their trees.

claims.statement: A 1995 United States Forest Service paper by forester Bruce G. Marcot claims the chickcharney legend was likely based on the prehistoric barn owl species Tyto pollens.
claims.statement_id: Makalah United States Forest Service 1995 oleh Bruce G. Marcot menyatakan legenda chickcharney kemungkinan didasarkan pada spesies burung hantu serak prasejarah Tyto pollens.
claims.quote: A 1995 United States Forest Service paper by forester Bruce G. Marcot claims that the legend of the chickcharney was likely based on the prehistoric barn owl species Tyto pollens

claims.statement: Marcot writes that the owl probably gave rise to local lore of chickcharnies, a mischievous leprechaunlike, nocturnal imp said to have three toes and to turn its head all the way around.
claims.statement_id: Marcot menulis bahwa burung hantu itu kemungkinan melahirkan kisah lokal tentang chickcharney, peri usil mirip leprechaun yang nokturnal, konon berjari kaki tiga dan dapat memutar kepala penuh.
claims.quote: It probably gave rise to local lore of chickcharnies, a mischievous leprechaunlike, nocturnal imp said to have three toes and the ability to turn its head all the way around.

claims.statement: According to Marcot, if disturbed, chickcharnies would impart terrible misfortune.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Marcot, jika diganggu, chickcharney akan mendatangkan kemalangan yang mengerikan.
claims.quote: If disturbed, chickcharnies would impart terrible misfortune.

claims.statement: Marcot suggests that the territorial defense behaviors of a meter-tall Tyto could give rise to such legends.
claims.statement_id: Marcot menduga perilaku mempertahankan wilayah dari burung Tyto setinggi satu meter dapat melahirkan legenda semacam itu.
claims.quote: It is possible that territorial defense behaviors of a meter-tall Tyto could give rise to such legends.

claims.statement: Paleontologist Lisa G. Buckley said the theory was likely true because T. pollens overlapped geographically and in time with the origin of the chickcharney myth.
claims.statement_id: Paleontolog Lisa G. Buckley menyatakan teori itu kemungkinan benar karena T. pollens tumpang tindih secara geografis dan waktu dengan asal mitos chickcharney.
claims.quote: Paleontologist Lisa G. Buckley claimed that this theory was likely true, stating that T. pollens had a geographical and temporal overlap with the origin of the chickcharney myth.

claims.statement: In Mixtec mythology, Dzahui (also Dzavui) is the rain god, offered child sacrifices on hilltops in times of drought, disease and harvest.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Mixtec, Dzahui (juga Dzavui) adalah dewa hujan yang dipersembahi korban anak di puncak bukit saat kemarau, wabah, dan panen.
claims.quote: In Mixtec mythology, Dzahui (also spelled Dzavui) is the god of rain, for whom child sacrifices were performed on hilltops during times of drought, disease, and harvest.

claims.statement: In Mixtec codices Dzahui wears the blue or green rain goggle mask also seen on Tlaloc.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kodeks Mixtec, Dzahui memakai topeng kacamata hujan biru atau hijau yang juga terlihat pada dewa Tlaloc.
claims.quote: In Mixtec codices, Dzahui exhibits the blue or green rain goggle mask also seen on the central Mexican deity Tlaloc.

claims.statement: Dzahui is depicted with exposed incisor teeth and longer, somewhat curled jaguar canine teeth emerging from curled lips.
claims.statement_id: Dzahui digambarkan memiliki gigi seri yang terlihat dan taring jaguar yang lebih panjang dan agak melengkung keluar dari bibir yang melengkung.
claims.quote: He possesses exposed teeth incisors and longer, somewhat curled jaguar canine teeth emerging from curled lips.

claims.statement: The tutelary god of the Mixtecs was Dzahui (literally "Rain"), divinity of rain and celestial water.
claims.statement_id: Dewa pelindung bangsa Mixtec adalah Dzahui (secara harfiah "Hujan"), dewa hujan dan air langit.
claims.quote: The tutelary god of the Mixtecs was Dzahui (literally Rain), divinity of rain and celestial water.

claims.statement: The cult of rain was so important to the Mixtecs that their native name means "people of the rain", that is, the people chosen by Dzahui.
claims.statement_id: Pemujaan hujan begitu penting bagi bangsa Mixtec sehingga nama asli mereka berarti "bangsa hujan", yakni bangsa yang dipilih Dzahui.
claims.quote: The cult of rain was so important for the Mixtecs that their native name qualifies them as the people of rain, that is, the people chosen by Dzahui.

claims.statement: He shares many attributes with Tlaloc of central Mesoamerica, who was venerated by the Teotihuacan, Toltec, and Mexica and appears on numerous effigy vessels found especially in Highland Mixteca.
claims.statement_id: Dzahui memiliki banyak atribut yang sama dengan Tlaloc dari Mesoamerika tengah, yang dipuja bangsa Teotihuacan, Toltek, dan Mexica serta tampak pada banyak bejana efigi, terutama di dataran tinggi Mixteca.
claims.quote: He shares many attributes with the Tlaloc of central Mesoamerica, venerated by the Teotihuacan, Toltec, and Mexica and who appears on numerous effigy vessels found especially in Highland Mixteca.

claims.statement: The cult of Dzahui among the Mixtec is very ancient, appearing at the end of the Late Preclassic, between the 5th century BC and the 2nd century AD.
claims.statement_id: Pemujaan Dzahui di kalangan Mixtec sangat tua, muncul sejak akhir masa Praklasik Akhir, yakni antara abad ke-5 SM dan abad ke-2 M.
claims.quote: The cult of Dzahui in the Mixtec is very ancient, its appearance dates back to the end of the Late Preclassic, that is, between the 5th century BC and 2nd century AD.

claims.statement: World History Encyclopedia states that in the various Mesoamerican cultures Tláloc appears as Dzahui for the Mixtec and as Cocijo for the Zapotec.
claims.statement_id: World History Encyclopedia menyebut bahwa dalam berbagai budaya Mesoamerika Tláloc tampil sebagai Dzahui bagi bangsa Mixtec dan sebagai Cocijo bagi bangsa Zapotec.
claims.quote: In the various Mesoamerican cultures Tláloc appears as Dzahui for the Mixtec, ... Cocijo for the Zapotec.

claims.statement: In Inuit mythology, Eeyeekalduk was the god of medicine and good health.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Inuit, Eeyeekalduk adalah dewa pengobatan dan kesehatan.
claims.quote: In Inuit mythology, Eeyeekalduk was the god of medicine and good health.

claims.statement: The Big Myth records Eeyeekalduk as the god of healing.
claims.statement_id: The Big Myth mencatat Eeyeekalduk sebagai dewa penyembuhan.
claims.quote: EEYEEKALDUK was the god of healing.

claims.statement: According to The Big Myth, the Inuit pantheon varies slightly depending on where the particular Inuit live.
claims.statement_id: Menurut The Big Myth, panteon Inuit sedikit berbeda tergantung tempat tinggal kelompok Inuit tertentu.
claims.quote: The Inuit Pantheon varies slightly, depending on where the particular Inuit live.

claims.statement: Wikipedia lists Eeyeekalduk under Inuit in its list of health deities, as god of medicine and good health.
claims.statement_id: Wikipedia mencantumkan Eeyeekalduk di bagian Inuit pada daftar dewa kesehatan, sebagai dewa pengobatan dan kesehatan yang baik.
claims.quote: Eeyeekalduk, god of medicine and good health

claims.statement: Inuit religion is the traditional religion of certain circumpolar peoples, practised in Inuit communities in parts of Chukotka, Alaska, northern Canada, and Greenland.
claims.statement_id: Agama Inuit adalah agama tradisional sejumlah bangsa di sekitar kutub yang dianut di komunitas Inuit di sebagian Chukotka, Alaska, Kanada utara, dan Greenland.
claims.quote: Inuit religion is the traditional religion of certain circumpolar peoples. It is practised within Inuit communities in parts of Chukotka, Alaska, northern Canada, and Greenland.

claims.statement: In Inuit religion, ritual specialists known as angakut mediated between humanity and the spirits and performed rituals for healing.
claims.statement_id: Dalam agama Inuit, pakar ritual yang disebut angakut berperan menjadi perantara antara manusia dan roh, dan mereka melakukan ritual penyembuhan.
claims.quote: an important role was played by ritual specialists known as angakut (sing. angakoq), who mediated between humanity and the spirits. They performed rituals for healing

claims.statement: El Hombre Caimán ("The Alligator Man") is an urban legend of the Caribbean coast of Colombia, set in Plato: Saúl Montenegro, who spied on bathing women, became a being with a man's head and an alligator's body.
claims.statement_id: El Hombre Caimán ("Manusia Buaya") adalah legenda urban pesisir Karibia Kolombia di kota Plato: Saúl Montenegro yang gemar mengintip perempuan mandi berubah menjadi makhluk berkepala manusia dan bertubuh buaya.
claims.quote: El Hombre Caimán (The Alligator Man) is an urban legend from the Caribbean coast of Colombia that takes place in the riverside town of Plato: Saúl Montenegro's passion for spying on naked women turned into a being with the head of a man and the body of an alligator.

claims.statement: The story was reportedly in the press in the 1940s.
claims.statement_id: Kisah ini konon diberitakan pers pada tahun 1940-an.
claims.quote: The story was allegedly reported in the press in the 1940s.

claims.statement: A witch gave him two potions: a red one to become an alligator and a white one to change back.
claims.statement_id: Seorang penyihir memberinya dua ramuan: merah untuk berubah menjadi buaya, dan putih untuk kembali.
claims.quote: The witch gave him two potions: a red one that turned him into an alligator, and a white one that turned him back.

claims.statement: Montenegro went to an indigenous woman (also called a brujo "witch" or piache "shaman") in Alta Guajira for a potion to turn into an alligator so the bathers would not suspect him.
claims.statement_id: Montenegro mendatangi seorang perempuan pribumi (juga disebut brujo "penyihir" atau piache "dukun") di Alta Guajira untuk meminta ramuan agar berubah menjadi buaya supaya para perempuan yang mandi tidak curiga.
claims.quote: went to an indio woman (also called a brujo "witch" or piache "shaman") in Alta Guajira for a potion to turn himself into an alligator so that the bathers would not suspect him and he could admire them as much as he wished.

claims.statement: A substitute who was to splash the white potion got scared and smashed the bottle, so only some liquid hit Saúl's head: his head returned to human but his body remained alligator.
claims.statement_id: Seorang pengganti yang bertugas memercikkan ramuan putih ketakutan dan memecahkan botolnya, sehingga hanya sebagian cairan mengenai kepala Saúl: kepalanya kembali manusia, tetapi tubuhnya tetap buaya.
claims.quote: the duty of splashing the white medicine to turn the caiman back into human fell on a substitute. But as he was not used to confronting the man in his alligator form, he got scared and smashed the bottle of white potion, so that only some of the liquid got splashed on Saúl's head, so his head returned to human, but his body remained alligator.

claims.statement: Left alone, the Alligator Man let the river carry him out to sea at Bocas de Ceniza, the mouth of the Magdalena River near Barranquilla.
claims.statement_id: Setelah ditinggalkan sendirian, Manusia Buaya membiarkan sungai membawanya ke laut di Bocas de Ceniza, muara Sungai Magdalena dekat Barranquilla.
claims.quote: Alligator Man was left alone, with no-one to take care of him. He decided to let the river carry him out to sea at Bocas de Ceniza the mouth of the Magdalena River, near Barranquilla.

claims.statement: A festival of the Alligator Man is held annually in Plato; a square and a monument were built in his honor and are part of local cultural heritage.
claims.statement_id: Festival Manusia Buaya digelar setiap tahun di Plato; sebuah alun-alun dan monumen dibangun untuk menghormatinya dan menjadi bagian warisan budaya setempat.
claims.quote: A festival of Alligator Man is held annually in Plato. A square and a monument have been built in his honor and are part of the local cultural heritage.

claims.statement: His legend is immortalized in the song "Se va el caimán" by Barranquilla musician José María Peñaranda.
claims.statement_id: Legendanya diabadikan dalam lagu "Se va el caimán" karya musisi Barranquilla José María Peñaranda.
claims.quote: His legend is immortalized in the song "Se va el caimán" by Barranquilla musician José María Peñaranda.

claims.statement: According to a legend of Plato, a man named Saúl Montenegro hid in the water to watch women bathing in the river, and so he was called "El Hombre Caimán".
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda Plato, seorang pria bernama Saúl Montenegro bersembunyi di air untuk mengintip perempuan yang mandi di sungai, sehingga ia dijuluki "El Hombre Caimán".
claims.quote: según una leyenda plateña, un hombre llamado Saúl Montenegro se escondía en las aguas para ver a las mujeres que se bañaban en el río y por eso se le llamó “El Hombre Caimán”

claims.statement: The Festival del Hombre Caimán in Plato runs from 16 to 20 December.
claims.statement_id: Festival del Hombre Caimán di Plato berlangsung pada 16–20 Desember.
claims.quote: el Festival del Hombre Caimán, del 16 al 20 de diciembre

claims.statement: In February 2024 Senator Carlos Mario Farelo filed two bills (Nos. 237 and 238 of 2024) so that the Festival del Hombre Caimán of Plato, Magdalena, be honored as a national heritage.
claims.statement_id: Pada Februari 2024, Senator Carlos Mario Farelo mengajukan dua rancangan undang-undang (No. 237 dan 238 tahun 2024) agar Festival del Hombre Caimán di Plato, Magdalena, diakui sebagai warisan bangsa.
claims.quote: Carlos Mario Farelo, del Partido Cambio Radical, radicó dos proyectos de ley, el 237 y 238 de 2024 ante la Secretaría General del Senado de la República para que el Festival del Hombre Caimán del municipio de Plato en el departamento del Magdalena, sea honrado como patrimonio de la Nación.

claims.statement: The story was allegedly published in the 1940s in the local paper La Prensa of Barranquilla, but the paper is defunct and recent informants who remembered the clippings could not be found.
claims.statement_id: Kisah ini konon dimuat pada 1940-an di surat kabar lokal La Prensa di Barranquilla, tetapi surat kabar itu sudah tidak terbit dan informan masa kini yang mengingat kliping itu tidak ditemukan.
claims.quote: This story allegedly was published during the 1940s in the local paper La Prensa of Barranquilla, but the newspaper is defunct, and informants in recent years could not be found who remembered reading the newspaper clippings.

claims.statement: The Enfield Monster is an unidentified creature reported around Enfield, Illinois, in April 1973.
claims.statement_id: Enfield Monster adalah makhluk tak dikenal yang dilaporkan di sekitar Enfield, Illinois, pada April 1973.
claims.quote: The Enfield Monster is an unidentified creature reported around Enfield, Illinois, United States in April 1973.

claims.statement: The media covered the reports, some suggesting a wild ape or escaped kangaroo.
claims.statement_id: Laporannya diberitakan media, dan sebagian menduga penyebabnya kera liar atau kanguru yang lepas.
claims.quote: The reports were covered by the news media at the time, with some suggesting they may have been caused by a wild ape or escaped kangaroo.

claims.statement: Sociologists cite the episode as an example of collective behavior.
claims.statement_id: Para sosiolog mengutip peristiwa ini sebagai contoh perilaku kolektif.
claims.quote: the episode is cited by sociologists as an example of collective behavior

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, at about 10 pm on April 25, 1973, Henry McDaniel heard a scratching sound at his front door.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, sekitar pukul 22.00 pada 25 April 1973 Henry McDaniel mendengar suara garukan di pintu depannya.
claims.quote: At about 10pm on the night of April 25, 1973, Henry McDaniel heard a scratching sound at his front door.

claims.statement: McDaniel later said the creature had three legs, a short body, two little short arms, and pink eyes as big as flashlights, stood four and a half feet tall, and was grayish.
claims.statement_id: McDaniel kemudian menyatakan makhluk itu berkaki tiga, bertubuh pendek, berlengan pendek kecil, bermata merah muda sebesar senter, setinggi empat setengah kaki, dan berwarna keabu-abuan.
claims.quote: It had three legs on it, a short body, two little short arms, and two pink eyes as big as flashlights. It stood four and a half feet tall and was grayish-colored.

claims.statement: According to the PBS Monstrum transcript, Henry described the creature as pink-eyed, large-headed, dirty gray, hairy, and about four or five feet tall.
claims.statement_id: Menurut transkrip PBS Monstrum, Henry menggambarkan makhluk itu bermata merah muda, berkepala besar, berwarna abu-abu kusam, berbulu, dan setinggi sekitar empat atau lima kaki.
claims.quote: Henry described the creature as having pink eyes, a large head, was a dirty-ish gray color, hairy, about four or five feet tall.

claims.statement: According to PBS, the search revealed tracks in the ground that looked like a dog's paw but with six toe pads.
claims.statement_id: Menurut PBS, penyelidikan menemukan jejak di tanah yang tampak seperti telapak anjing tetapi dengan enam bantalan jari.
claims.quote: Their search revealed tracks in the ground that looked like a dog's paw, but with six toe pads.

claims.statement: The researchers found no more than three firsthand reports, later exaggerated by news stories and local gossip into an "epidemic."
claims.statement_id: Para peneliti menemukan tidak lebih dari tiga laporan langsung yang kemudian dibesar-besarkan oleh pemberitaan dan gosip setempat menjadi "epidemi".
claims.quote: The researchers found there were no more than three firsthand reports that had subsequently been exaggerated by news stories and local gossip into an "epidemic."

claims.statement: According to PBS, a letter was sent to a nearby newspaper by a man claiming his pet kangaroo Macey had gone missing about a year earlier in Ohio.
claims.statement_id: Menurut PBS, sebuah surat dikirim ke surat kabar setempat oleh seorang pria yang mengaku kanguru peliharaannya bernama Macey hilang sekitar setahun sebelumnya di Ohio.
claims.quote: a letter was sent to a nearby newspaper from a man claiming that his pet kangaroo Macey had gone missing about a year prior in Ohio.

claims.statement: According to PBS, the sociologists concluded that Enfield was not a classic case of mass hysteria.
claims.statement_id: Menurut PBS, para sosiolog menyimpulkan bahwa Enfield bukan kasus klasik histeria massa.
claims.quote: The sociologists concluded that Enfield was not a classic case of mass hysteria.

claims.statement: In 1978 researchers at Western Illinois University headed by David L. Miller investigated and analyzed the incident, publishing it as a case study in social contagion.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1978 peneliti Western Illinois University yang dipimpin David L. Miller menyelidiki dan menganalisis peristiwa itu, lalu menerbitkannya sebagai studi kasus penularan sosial.
claims.quote: In 1978 researchers at Western Illinois University headed by David L. Miller investigated and analyzed the incident, publishing it as a case study in social contagion.

claims.statement: Two weeks later, on May 6, McDaniel called radio station WWKI claiming to have seen the creature again at 3 a.m. that morning.
claims.statement_id: Dua minggu kemudian, pada 6 Mei, McDaniel menelepon stasiun radio WWKI dan mengaku melihat makhluk itu lagi pada pukul 03.00 pagi itu.
claims.quote: Two weeks later on May 6, McDaniel called the radio station WWKI claiming to have seen the creature again, at 3 a.m. that morning.

claims.statement: According to PBS, that was the first night of what would become known as the Enfield Horror.
claims.statement_id: Menurut PBS, malam itu adalah malam pertama dari peristiwa yang kemudian dikenal sebagai Enfield Horror.
claims.quote: It was the first night in what would become known as the Enfield Horror.

claims.statement: Gaasyendietha, the "meteor dragon" of Seneca mythology, is a giant serpent living in the depths of Canadian rivers and lakes, especially Lake Ontario.
claims.statement_id: Gaasyendietha, "naga meteor" dalam mitologi Seneca, adalah ular raksasa yang tinggal di bagian dalam sungai dan danau Kanada, terutama Danau Ontario.
claims.quote: also known as the meteor dragon according to Seneca mythology, is a giant serpent that dwells in the deep areas of rivers and lakes of Canada, especially Lake Ontario.

claims.statement: It could fly on a trail of fire and spew fire, so it is likened to European dragons.
claims.statement_id: Ular ini dapat terbang di atas jejak api dan menyemburkan api, sehingga disamakan dengan naga Eropa.
claims.quote: This serpent could fly on a trail of fire, and it could also spew fire, which has led to it being viewed as analogous to European dragons.

claims.statement: The name "meteor dragon" refers to its supposed origin in a meteoroid that struck Earth.
claims.statement_id: Julukan "naga meteor" merujuk pada asal-usulnya dari meteoroid yang menghantam Bumi.
claims.quote: in reference to its supposed origin from a meteoroid that had impacted the Earth.

claims.statement: According to the Seneca, Gaasyendietha, a fire-breathing dragon, lives in lakes and rivers in Canada, in particular Lake Ontario.
claims.statement_id: Menurut orang Seneca, Gaasyendietha, naga penyembur api, hidup di danau dan sungai di Kanada, khususnya Danau Ontario.
claims.quote: According to the Seneca, Gaasyendietha, a fire-breathing dragon, lives in lakes and rivers in Canada, in particular Lake Ontario.

claims.statement: Seneca oral tradition proposed two possible origins for Gaasyendietha: born from a serpent's eggs, or fallen to Earth from a meteor.
claims.statement_id: Tradisi lisan Seneca mengajukan dua kemungkinan asal Gaasyendietha: lahir dari telur ular, atau jatuh ke Bumi dari meteor.
claims.quote: The Seneca oral tradition proposed two possible origins for Gaasyendietha: either the dragon was born from a serpent's eggs, or it fell to the Earth from a meteor.

claims.statement: Due to its possible meteoric origins it is sometimes called the "meteor dragon" and was supposed to be able to fly across the sky on a stream of fire.
claims.statement_id: Karena kemungkinan asal meteoriknya, ia kadang disebut "naga meteor" dan dipercaya dapat terbang melintasi langit di atas aliran api.
claims.quote: Due to Gaasyendietha's possible meteoric origins, it is sometimes referred to as "meteor dragon" and was supposed to be able to fly across the sky on a stream of fire.

claims.statement: The encyclopedia notes that many Native American nations used myths to explain natural phenomena, so it has been suggested that the tale of Gaasyendietha explained the presence of meteors.
claims.statement_id: Ensiklopedia itu menyebut banyak bangsa asli Amerika memakai mitos untuk menjelaskan gejala alam, sehingga ada usulan bahwa kisah Gaasyendietha dibuat untuk menjelaskan keberadaan meteor.
claims.quote: Many of the Native American nations used myths to explain natural phenomena. Thus, the suggestion has been made that the tale of Gaasyendietha was created as a way to explain the presence of meteors.

claims.statement: The Seneca, once one of the largest of the Iroquois tribes, originally lived in the areas now known as Ontario, Canada, and New York State.
claims.statement_id: Orang Seneca, dahulu salah satu suku Iroquois terbesar, semula tinggal di wilayah yang kini dikenal sebagai Ontario, Kanada, dan Negara Bagian New York.
claims.quote: The Seneca, once one of the largest of the Iroquois tribes, originally lived in the areas now recognized as Ontario, Canada, and New York State.

claims.statement: The Seneca spoke of Gaasyendietha, an enormous hydra snake that could breathe fire and fly like a bird.
claims.statement_id: Orang Seneca bercerita tentang Gaasyendietha, ular hidra raksasa yang dapat menyemburkan api dan terbang seperti burung.
claims.quote: The Seneca spoke of Gaasyendietha, an enormous hydra snake that could breathe fire and fly like a bird.

claims.statement: According to the article, the explorer Jacques Cartier encountered something strange in the St. Lawrence River.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel itu, penjelajah Jacques Cartier menjumpai sesuatu yang aneh di Sungai St. Lawrence.
claims.quote: Even Jacques Cartier, best-known for exploring and mapping the Gulf of Saint Lawrence, encountered something strange in the St. Lawrence River.

claims.statement: When Cartier told the local First Nations people what he had seen, they referred to the "snake" as "Gaasyendietha".
claims.statement_id: Ketika Cartier menceritakan apa yang dilihatnya kepada penduduk Bangsa Pertama setempat, mereka menyebut "ular" itu sebagai "Gaasyendietha".
claims.quote: When Cartier told the First Nations people in the area about what he had seen, they knowingly referred to the “snake” as “Gaasyendietha.”

claims.statement: In his journal Cartier noted that he and his crew saw "a giant finned snake" moving through the water like a caterpillar, pushing itself forward with its side fins.
claims.statement_id: Dalam jurnalnya, Cartier mencatat bahwa ia dan awaknya melihat "ular raksasa bersirip" bergerak di air seperti ulat, mendorong diri ke depan dengan sirip sampingnya.
claims.quote: In his journal, Cartier noted that he and his crew witnessed “a giant finned snake” moving through the water like a caterpillar, thrusting itself forward with its side fins.

claims.statement: In some versions of the Haudenosaunee creation story, Gaasyendietha caught Atahensic as she fell to earth from the Sky World.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian versi kisah penciptaan Haudenosaunee, Gaasyendietha menangkap Atahensic saat ia jatuh ke bumi dari Dunia Langit.
claims.quote: In some versions of the Haudenosaunee creation story, Gaasyendietha caught Atahensic as she fell to earth from the Sky World.

claims.statement: In the tale "Ganyadjigowa", the hero Ganyadjigowa (The Mudhen) was killed by Gaasyendietha in the form of an old man.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah "Ganyadjigowa", sang pahlawan Ganyadjigowa (Si Mudhen) dibunuh oleh Gaasyendietha yang berwujud lelaki tua.
claims.quote: In the tale "Ganyadjigowa", the hero Ganyadjigowa (The Mudhen) was killed by Gaasyendietha, in the form of an old man.

claims.statement: Another name for it is the "fire lion", the Iroquoian version of the underwater panther.
claims.statement_id: Julukan lainnya adalah "singa api", versi Iroquois dari panter air (underwater panther).
claims.quote: Another reference to it is as the "fire lion", which is the Iroquioan version of the underwater panther.

claims.statement: Gaasyendietha is mentioned briefly in literary works such as Kim Jobe's The Guardians of Mandoria (2011) and Kathleen and Michael Gear's The Summoning God: Book II of the Anasazi Mysteries (2001).
claims.statement_id: Gaasyendietha disebut singkat dalam karya sastra seperti The Guardians of Mandoria (2011) karya Kim Jobe dan The Summoning God: Book II of the Anasazi Mysteries (2001) karya Kathleen dan Michael Gear.
claims.quote: Gaasyendietha is mentioned, although briefly, in literary works such as Kim Jobe's The Guardians of Mandoria (2011) and Kathleen and Michael Gear's The Summoning God: Book II of the Anasazi Mysteries (2001).

claims.statement: Jasy Jatere is an important figure of Guaraní mythology, one of the seven cursed children of Tau and Kerana and among the most important Guaraní gods, especially in Paraguay.
claims.statement_id: Jasy Jatere adalah tokoh penting mitologi Guaraní, salah satu dari tujuh anak terkutuk Tau dan Kerana, dan salah satu dewa terpenting bagi budaya berbahasa Guaraní, terutama di Paraguay.
claims.quote: is an important figure in Guaraní mythology. One of the seven cursed children of Tau and Kerana, Jasy Jatere is one of the most important gods among the Guaraní speaking cultures of South America, especially in Paraguay.

claims.statement: His name means "a little piece of the moon"; unlike his brothers, he is not monstrous.
claims.statement_id: Namanya berarti "sepotong kecil bulan"; ia satu-satunya di antara saudaranya yang tidak berwujud monster.
claims.quote: Jasy Jatere, which means literally "a little piece of the moon", is unique among his brothers in that he does not have a monstrous appearance.

claims.statement: He is usually a small man or child with light blond hair and sometimes blue eyes.
claims.statement_id: Ia biasanya digambarkan sebagai lelaki kecil atau anak berambut pirang terang, kadang bermata biru.
claims.quote: He is usually described as being a small man or perhaps a child, with light blonde hair and sometimes blue eyes.

claims.statement: According to the Museo Mitológico Ramón Elías text, he is the child-genius of hot siestas who wanders cheerfully through Guaraní forests and valleys and is the lord of the countryside siestas.
claims.statement_id: Menurut teks Museo Mitológico Ramón Elías, ia adalah anak-genius siesta yang panas, yang berkelana riang di hutan dan lembah Guaraní, dan tuan siesta di pedesaan.
claims.quote: Este niño-genio de las siestas calurosas que transita alegremente por las selvas y valles guaraníes, es el señor de las siestas campesinas.

claims.statement: According to the museum text, Jasy Jatere is almost always invisible, sending a sharp whistle into the wind.
claims.statement_id: Menurut teks museum, Jasy Jatere hampir selalu tak terlihat dan melepaskan siulan nyaring ke angin.
claims.quote: JASY JATERE casi siempre anda invisible lanzando al viento un agudo silbido.

claims.statement: According to the museum text, country people also consider him a protector of birds, wild fruits, and animals.
claims.statement_id: Menurut teks museum, orang desa juga menganggapnya pelindung burung, buah liar, dan hewan.
claims.quote: La gente del campo también le considera protector de las aves, de frutas silvestres y de los animales.

claims.statement: According to the museum text, Jasy Jatere's kiss burns and destroys like fire and no human being can bear it.
claims.statement_id: Menurut teks museum, ciuman Jasy Jatere membakar dan menghancurkan seperti api dan tak ada manusia yang sanggup menahannya.
claims.quote: Aquel beso quema y destruye como el fuego. Ningún ser humano puede soportarlo.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, Jasy Jatere is also considered the lord of the siesta, the traditional mid-day nap taken in many Latin American cultures.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, Jasy Jatere juga dianggap penguasa siesta, tidur siang tradisional di banyak budaya Amerika Latin.
claims.quote: Jasy Jatere is also considered to be the lord of the siesta, the traditional mid-day nap taken in many Latin American cultures.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, he is considered the protector of the yerba mate plant and sometimes also a protector of hidden treasures.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, ia dianggap pelindung tanaman yerba mate dan kadang juga pelindung harta terpendam.
claims.quote: he is considered to be the protector of the yerba mate plant. Sometimes he is also viewed as a protector of hidden treasures.

claims.statement: According to the Pérez-Maricevich compilation, Jasy jateré ("fragment of moon") is considered the Guaraní Cupid and bearer of fertility.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kompilasi Pérez-Maricevich, Jasy jateré ("fragmen bulan") dianggap Cupid Guaraní dan pembawa kesuburan.
claims.quote: A Jasy jateré (fragmento de luna) se lo considera el Cupido guaraní y portador de la fecundidad.

claims.statement: According to the compilation, he is believed to live in hollows of the trunks of large forest trees.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kompilasi itu, ia dipercaya tinggal di lubang batang pohon besar di hutan.
claims.quote: Se cree que vive en huecos de troncos de grandes árboles del bosque.

claims.statement: According to the compilation, Jasy-jateré attracts children with his whistle or by touching them with his staff.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kompilasi itu, Jasy-jateré memikat anak-anak dengan peluitnya atau dengan menyentuh mereka memakai tongkatnya.
claims.quote: El Jasy-jateré atrae a los niños con su silbato o tocándolos con su bastón

claims.statement: According to the compilation, he abducts children to the forest, keeps them for a time, feeds them wild honey and fruit, plays with them, and finally releases them or leaves them tangled in ysypó (liana).
claims.statement_id: Menurut kompilasi itu, ia menculik anak-anak ke hutan, menahan mereka beberapa waktu, memberi mereka madu liar dan buah, bermain dengan mereka, lalu melepaskan atau meninggalkan mereka tersangkut di liana ysypó.
claims.quote: Los rapta y los lleva al bosque dónde los retiene durante algún tiempo, los alimenta con miel silvestre y frutas, juega con ellos y al fin los suelta o los deja enredados en ysypó (liana)

claims.statement: According to the compilation, the children afterwards become foolish, mute, or deaf-mute, but recover after some time.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kompilasi itu, anak-anak itu kemudian menjadi dungu, bisu, atau tuli-bisu, tetapi pulih setelah beberapa waktu.
claims.quote: pero los niños ya se han vuelto tontos o idiotas (tavy: aka tavy), mudos (ne'engú) o sordomudos; se recuperan después de un cierto tiempo.

claims.statement: According to the compilation, when Yasy-jateré loses his little staff and whistle he becomes harmless, having lost his magic power.

claims.statement: Caicai was sent to care for the sea with the Ngen-ko water spirits, and Trentren to live on land.

claims.statement: According to the Museo Chileno de Arte Precolombino, Caicai and Trentren are two serpents in Mapuche stories; Caicai lives in the sea and Trentren resides on land.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Museo Chileno de Arte Precolombino, Caicai dan Trentren adalah dua ular dalam kisah-kisah Mapuche; Caicai hidup di laut dan Trentren berdiam di darat.
claims.quote: Caicai y Trentren son dos serpientes que aparecen en los relatos mapuches. Caicai vive en el mar y Trentren reside en la tierra.

claims.statement: According to the museum, the sea-quakes and earthquakes that periodically strike the territory are held to be manifestations of the antagonism between Caicai and Trentren.
claims.statement_id: Menurut museum itu, tsunami dan gempa bumi yang sesekali melanda wilayah itu dianggap sebagai perwujudan antagonisme antara Caicai dan Trentren.
claims.quote: Los maremotos y terremotos que asolan el territorio de tiempo en tiempo ... antagonismo entre Caicai y Trentren.

claims.statement: According to Chile Precolombino, an enormous serpent rose up from the sea and began crying "kai, kai, kai", louder and shriller.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Chile Precolombino, seekor ular raksasa muncul dari laut dan mulai berteriak "kai, kai, kai" makin keras dan makin melengking.
claims.quote: an enormous serpent rose up from the sea and began crying, kai, kai, kai, louder and louder, shriller and shriller.

claims.statement: According to Chile Precolombino, the Mapuche people ran to the mountaintops to save themselves.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Chile Precolombino, bangsa Mapuche berlari ke puncak gunung untuk menyelamatkan diri.
claims.quote: To save themselves, the Mapuche people ran to the mountaintops.

claims.statement: According to Chile Precolombino, the divine serpent came to help them, and thus began the battle between Kai Kai and Treng Treng.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Chile Precolombino, ular ilahi datang menolong mereka, dan begitulah pertarungan Kai Kai dan Treng Treng dimulai.
claims.quote: It was the divine serpent come to help them. And thus began the battle between Kai Kai and Treng Treng.

claims.statement: According to Chile Precolombino, seeing he was vanquished, Kai Kai sank back into the depths of the sea and has never been seen again.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Chile Precolombino, melihat dirinya terkalahkan, Kai Kai tenggelam kembali ke dasar laut dan tak pernah terlihat lagi.
claims.quote: Seeing he was vanquished, Kai Kai sank back into the depths of the sea, and has never been seen again.

claims.statement: According to Chile Precolombino, ever since, whenever the earth shakes and the sea floods the land, or the rain lashes down and rivers and lakes rise, the Mapuche hear Kai Kai's cry.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Chile Precolombino, sejak saat itu setiap kali bumi berguncang dan laut membanjiri daratan, atau hujan mendera dan sungai serta danau meluap, orang Mapuche mendengar teriakan Kai Kai.
claims.quote: since that time, whenever the earth shakes and the sea floods the land, or when the rain lashes down from the heavens and the rivers and lakes rise up, the Mapuches hear Kai Kai

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, the Mapuche say the two snakes were originally the children of the most powerful pillans, converted into their animal forms as punishment.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, orang Mapuche menyebut kedua ular itu semula anak-anak pillán yang paling berkuasa, yang diubah menjadi wujud hewan sebagai hukuman.
claims.quote: According to the Mapuche, the two snakes were originally the children of the most powerful pillans, who were converted into their animal forms as punishment.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, as the sea kept rising, Trentren had to order the hills to grow in height to counteract Caicai's power.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, ketika laut terus naik, Trentren harus memerintahkan bukit-bukit bertambah tinggi untuk melawan kekuatan Caicai.
claims.quote: But as the sea continued to rise, Trentren had to order the hills to increase in height to counteract the power of Caicai.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, in Chiloé tradition Caicai was satisfied with the land he had managed to flood and delegated his sea-related functions to the great Millalobo.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, dalam tradisi Chiloé Caicai puas dengan bagian daratan yang berhasil dibanjirinya dan menyerahkan tugas-tugasnya atas laut kepada Millalobo yang agung.
claims.quote: According to Chiloé tradition, Caicai was satisfied with the portion of land that he had managed to flood, and delegated his functions pertaining to the sea to the great Millalobo.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, in the Tolten region version Trentren was a hill and a good spirit that helped people, while Caicai was a sea bird, an evil spirit that harmed people.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, dalam versi wilayah Tolten Trentren adalah sebuah bukit sekaligus roh baik yang menolong manusia, sedangkan Caicai adalah burung laut, roh jahat yang mencelakai manusia.
claims.quote: Trentren was a hall and also a good spirit which helped people. Caicai was a sea bird, an evil spirit, who used to harm people.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, in Argentina there are other, later versions that change the original parents of the two snakes, indicating they are brothers and/or sons of the gods Nguenechèn and Kueyen.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, di Argentina ada versi lain yang lebih belakangan yang mengubah orang tua kedua ular itu, menyebut mereka saudara dan/atau anak para dewa Nguenechèn dan Kueyen.
claims.quote: In Argentina there are other later versions of the myth, which change the original parents of both mythical snakes, indicating that they would be brothers and/or sons of the gods Nguenechèn and Kueyen.
